It's simple: The Voting Rights Act was passed to outlaw racial discrimination in elections , including the drawing of districts in ways that effectively blocked minority groups from electing their preferred candidates.
Since the Supreme Court started gutting the VRA more than a decade ago, vote suppressors in state legislatures have used the redistricting process to silence minority voters by gerrymandering them into electoral irrelevance. Now the state of Georgia is fighting in court to win the right to do it with impunity and codify voter suppression into their maps forever.
We must spread the word and continue to fight for fair maps and our right to vote. RUSH $25 or more right now to fuel our work to protect voting rights in Georgia and beyond >> [https://secure.everyaction.com/pdjfDAEu4UCpXPQPEnrW-A2]
Voter Action Project
Atlanta Voice: Georgia seeks another Supreme Court showdown over Voting Rights Act
Bad news for everyone, Team: The state of Georgia is seeking another Supreme Court showdown over the Voting Rights Act, asking a federal appeals court to interpret the 1965 law in a way that could make it much harder to prove minority votes have been illegally diluted.
Georgia is trying persuade the judges to make up a new, harder-to-prove standard that could hobble Voting Rights Act lawsuits, less than two years after the U.S. Supreme Court turned back a separate challenge from Alabama to the VRA.
From the AP: " A lawyer for the state asked a three-judge panel of the 11th Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals in Atlanta to overturn a lower court that required lawmakers to draw more Black-majority electoral districts. Georgia’s Republican Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger argued in court filings that the Voting Rights Act is being misused to bolster Democratic election chances and that white voters prefer Republicans for nonracial reasons. "
Opponents of voting rights are hell-bent on dismantling the Voting Rights Act piece by piece and we can't let them. We have to fight in Georgia, Alabama, and beyond to protect our fundamental rights
Pitch in $25 or whatever you can today to give us the resources we need to defend our right to vote in the states, in the courts, and in Congress >> [https://secure.everyaction.com/pdjfDAEu4UCpXPQPEnrW-A2]

"**Texas Legislature approves $8.5 billion boost for public schools after years of stagnant funding,** " Texas Tribune's **Jaden Edison** - "The Texas House on Thursday gave the final stamp of approval to legislation authorizing roughly $8.5 billion in funding for public schools, sending the bill to Gov. **Greg Abbott 's** desk where it is soon expected to become law.

Final passage of [House Bill 2](https://substack.com/redirect/5154e7bd-bea9-4918-8c2d-f3da7fcab2db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which will give schools additional money for teacher and staff salaries, educator preparation, special education, safety requirements and early childhood learning, comes on the heels of [extensive negotiations](https://substack.com/redirect/db1b49bf-36ee-422d-b4ba-2be8bf1384cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) between the House and Senate over how the final version of the bill would look.

Abbott has already said he intends to sign the bill, a notable difference from two years ago when he and the Legislature withheld billions from public schools following a failed attempt to create a private school voucher program. This year, lawmakers vowed to approve vouchers and new public school funding in tandem. The Legislature finalized the education finance package on a 122-13 vote nearly a month after vouchers [officially became law](https://substack.com/redirect/616a48d4-a54c-4e62-94bc-90b552888208?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/ab2c1e6d-2e4a-4ef0-b8f7-962e1a52eace?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The new dollars in HB 2 will allow school districts to begin making a dent in some of their long-standing challenges -- a laundry list of items that includes reversing budget deficits, providing raises to full-time employees and keeping up with rising operational costs.

Before the legislation's final passage on Thursday, Rep. **James Talarico** , D-Austin, raised questions about the bill, underscoring that public schools' dire situation is partly the result of stagnant funding since 2019, the year lawmakers last raised schools' base dollars and passed a[ comprehensive education finance package](https://substack.com/redirect/4dbaeced-ec2e-4d57-9ced-347be5aa21c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/ab2c1e6d-2e4a-4ef0-b8f7-962e1a52eace?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
He sought to have Republican Rep. **Brad Buckley** of Salado, the bill sponsor, answer why the Republican-led Legislature has not passed major school funding legislation since then, including last session when the state had a [historic $32.7 billion budget surplus](https://substack.com/redirect/968e4434-2453-449d-b281-071a712cd847?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at its disposal.

The House public education chair only had a few moments to answer the question before lawmakers' speaking time expired, but his response instead focused on HB 2's investments in the basic costs of running a school and paying teachers what they deserve.

HB 2 will provide districts with a $55 per-student increase to their base funding -- a number short of the $395 per student hike proposed by the House earlier in the session and far less than the roughly $1,300 school officials said they needed to keep up with inflation. That base funding, known as the basic allotment, provides districts the most flexibility to address the range of needs on their campuses, from salaries and maintenance to instructional materials and athletics.

The bill raises educator pay, which represents more than $4 billion of the proposal's overall funding. To do so, it dictates:

> Teachers with three to four years of experience in school districts with 5,000 or fewer students will receive a $4,000 raise, while those with five or more years of teaching on their resume will earn $8,000.

> Teachers with three to four years of experience in school districts with more than 5,000 students will earn a $2,500 raise, while those with five or more years of experience will receive $5,000.

HB 2 also includes funding for an expansion of the Teacher Incentive Allotment, [a state program](https://substack.com/redirect/cc43bdc9-d6b8-4b10-b701-128a8bcfcc30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that awards raises to educators who demonstrate that they have improved their students' academic outcomes -- currently about 6% of teachers.

In place of a significant boost to the basic allotment, the bill will give districts $45 per student that they can only use to increase the salaries of school counselors, librarians, nurses and other support staff. The bill also grants schools $106 per student to pay costs associated with transportation, insurance, utilities and hiring retired educators, which has become more common as schools struggle to fill teacher vacancies.

Furthermore, the legislation will overhaul Texas' [special education funding system](https://substack.com/redirect/af779b10-c82c-4199-b526-23cbaeb830a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to account for the individual needs of each student; establish a compensation system for [educator preparation](https://substack.com/redirect/1fd3fcc2-1bcf-49eb-bb18-22dace57b9a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and mentorship programs; set aside money for schools to better identify learning difficulties among the state's [youngest students](https://substack.com/redirect/e0dd39bb-b95a-4bc2-a32a-5a870a423303?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and fund prekindergarten services; and increase the money districts receive for [safety upgrades](https://substack.com/redirect/98694bb5-c718-413a-a09a-eb5b5722acd1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." Greg Abbott 's desk where it is soon expected to become law. Final passage of , which will give schools additional money for teacher and staff salaries, educator preparation, special education, safety requirements and early childhood learning, comes on the heels of between the House and Senate over how the final version of the bill would look. Abbott has already said he intends to sign the bill, a notable difference from two years ago when he and the Legislature withheld billions from public schools following a failed attempt to create a private school voucher program. This year, lawmakers vowed to approve vouchers and new public school funding in tandem. The Legislature finalized the education finance package on a 122-13 vote nearly a month after vouchers . The new dollars in HB 2 will allow school districts to begin making a dent in some of their long-standing challenges -- a laundry list of items that includes reversing budget deficits, providing raises to full-time employees and keeping up with rising operational costs. Before the legislation's final passage on Thursday, Rep. James Talarico , D-Austin, raised questions about the bill, underscoring that public schools' dire situation is partly the result of stagnant funding since 2019, the year lawmakers last raised schools' base dollars and passed a. He sought to have Republican Rep. Brad Buckley of Salado, the bill sponsor, answer why the Republican-led Legislature has not passed major school funding legislation since then, including last session when the state had a at its disposal. The House public education chair only had a few moments to answer the question before lawmakers' speaking time expired, but his response instead focused on HB 2's investments in the basic costs of running a school and paying teachers what they deserve. HB 2 will provide districts with a $55 per-student increase to their base funding -- a number short of the $395 per student hike proposed by the House earlier in the session and far less than the roughly $1,300 school officials said they needed to keep up with inflation. That base funding, known as the basic allotment, provides districts the most flexibility to address the range of needs on their campuses, from salaries and maintenance to instructional materials and athletics. The bill raises educator pay, which represents more than $4 billion of the proposal's overall funding. To do so, it dictates: Teachers with three to four years of experience in school districts with 5,000 or fewer students will receive a $4,000 raise, while those with five or more years of teaching on their resume will earn $8,000. Teachers with three to four years of experience in school districts with more than 5,000 students will earn a $2,500 raise, while those with five or more years of experience will receive $5,000. HB 2 also includes funding for an expansion of the Teacher Incentive Allotment, that awards raises to educators who demonstrate that they have improved their students' academic outcomes -- currently about 6% of teachers. In place of a significant boost to the basic allotment, the bill will give districts $45 per student that they can only use to increase the salaries of school counselors, librarians, nurses and other support staff. The bill also grants schools $106 per student to pay costs associated with transportation, insurance, utilities and hiring retired educators, which has become more common as schools struggle to fill teacher vacancies. Furthermore, the legislation will overhaul Texas' to account for the individual needs of each student; establish a compensation system for and mentorship programs; set aside money for schools to better identify learning difficulties among the state's and fund prekindergarten services; and increase the money districts receive for ." Peter —
I know you get a lot of emails from me. But I want to take a few minutes to tell you about my decision to run for governor, and why your support is so critical to our success.
**I was raised to believe that we have an obligation to our community and our country.** This country gave my family so much, and it’s always been obvious to me that I wanted to dedicate my life to public service.
It’s why I took my first oath to the Constitution as a teenager when I entered the Naval Academy.
It’s why I spent nearly a decade in the Navy as a helicopter pilot and Russian policy officer.
It’s why I went to law school, and became an Outreach and Reentry Coordinator and a federal prosecutor.
**Peter, it’s why I first decided to run for office.**
In 2017, I watched Donald Trump attack every value that I had spent my life fighting for. And as I thought about it, I realized I couldn’t ask someone to do my fighting for me – that if I wanted to defend the country I love then I had to run toward the crisis.
It was a long shot to run as a nobody in a district that had been held by an entrenched Republican for more than two decades.
**But I knew what was at stake and I knew what I had to do.**
I’m proud of the work I’ve done in Congress — work that earned me the distinction of being named the most effective member of the New Jersey House delegation in just my second term.
**But I know I can do more as your governor. And that’s why I decided to run.**
By winning this seat, we can build more homes to reduce mortgage and rental costs, crack down on shady middlemen making prescription medications more expensive, and bring down utility costs by bringing more clean, cheap power like solar onto the grid.
But the truth is that this is already the most expensive New Jersey gubernatorial race on record. And our opponents are benefiting from millions of dollars in spending from outside entities. So I am asking:
**[Will you consider splitting $10 or whatever you can between my campaign and Heartland Patriots as we head into the final stretch before the June 10 election?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/88600?refcode=em20250529-8971&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=8971%2E614464%2Eccj8hL)**

"**Texas Legislature approves $8.5 billion boost for public schools after years of stagnant funding,** " Texas Tribune's **Jaden Edison** - "The Texas House on Thursday gave the final stamp of approval to legislation authorizing roughly $8.5 billion in funding for public schools, sending the bill to Gov. **Greg Abbott 's** desk where it is soon expected to become law.

Final passage of [House Bill 2](https://substack.com/redirect/8a80697b-df6e-454c-9eac-a6b232b2eabf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which will give schools additional money for teacher and staff salaries, educator preparation, special education, safety requirements and early childhood learning, comes on the heels of [extensive negotiations](https://substack.com/redirect/205696d3-a437-461c-8439-8d7243c387fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) between the House and Senate over how the final version of the bill would look.

Abbott has already said he intends to sign the bill, a notable difference from two years ago when he and the Legislature withheld billions from public schools following a failed attempt to create a private school voucher program. This year, lawmakers vowed to approve vouchers and new public school funding in tandem. The Legislature finalized the education finance package on a 122-13 vote nearly a month after vouchers [officially became law](https://substack.com/redirect/d17ff09c-312f-4b1f-9362-dd449c452f2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/6ba09469-6058-4f60-9621-32c007aefc7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The new dollars in HB 2 will allow school districts to begin making a dent in some of their long-standing challenges -- a laundry list of items that includes reversing budget deficits, providing raises to full-time employees and keeping up with rising operational costs.

Before the legislation's final passage on Thursday, Rep. **James Talarico** , D-Austin, raised questions about the bill, underscoring that public schools' dire situation is partly the result of stagnant funding since 2019, the year lawmakers last raised schools' base dollars and passed a[ comprehensive education finance package](https://substack.com/redirect/192c8a66-aed8-4ce3-ba10-71670ff1c9b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/6ba09469-6058-4f60-9621-32c007aefc7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
He sought to have Republican Rep. **Brad Buckley** of Salado, the bill sponsor, answer why the Republican-led Legislature has not passed major school funding legislation since then, including last session when the state had a [historic $32.7 billion budget surplus](https://substack.com/redirect/c2b3021d-a96a-4439-bd97-5b09fb56cede?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at its disposal.

The House public education chair only had a few moments to answer the question before lawmakers' speaking time expired, but his response instead focused on HB 2's investments in the basic costs of running a school and paying teachers what they deserve.

HB 2 will provide districts with a $55 per-student increase to their base funding -- a number short of the $395 per student hike proposed by the House earlier in the session and far less than the roughly $1,300 school officials said they needed to keep up with inflation. That base funding, known as the basic allotment, provides districts the most flexibility to address the range of needs on their campuses, from salaries and maintenance to instructional materials and athletics.

The bill raises educator pay, which represents more than $4 billion of the proposal's overall funding. To do so, it dictates:

> Teachers with three to four years of experience in school districts with 5,000 or fewer students will receive a $4,000 raise, while those with five or more years of teaching on their resume will earn $8,000.

> Teachers with three to four years of experience in school districts with more than 5,000 students will earn a $2,500 raise, while those with five or more years of experience will receive $5,000.

HB 2 also includes funding for an expansion of the Teacher Incentive Allotment, [a state program](https://substack.com/redirect/4aa5bce2-6baa-4116-b503-c40dc159ad41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that awards raises to educators who demonstrate that they have improved their students' academic outcomes -- currently about 6% of teachers.

In place of a significant boost to the basic allotment, the bill will give districts $45 per student that they can only use to increase the salaries of school counselors, librarians, nurses and other support staff. The bill also grants schools $106 per student to pay costs associated with transportation, insurance, utilities and hiring retired educators, which has become more common as schools struggle to fill teacher vacancies.

Furthermore, the legislation will overhaul Texas' [special education funding system](https://substack.com/redirect/f7f45562-ca65-49fd-bced-66854f9eed75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to account for the individual needs of each student; establish a compensation system for [educator preparation](https://substack.com/redirect/6490c357-cef1-449a-a11e-564bad9b7d99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and mentorship programs; set aside money for schools to better identify learning difficulties among the state's [youngest students](https://substack.com/redirect/068d1696-8a0c-4550-880f-e3693736cc93?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and fund prekindergarten services; and increase the money districts receive for [safety upgrades](https://substack.com/redirect/d9b72f62-505c-4c88-999f-ad470e96207c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." Final passage of , which will give schools additional money for teacher and staff salaries, educator preparation, special education, safety requirements and early childhood learning, comes on the heels of between the House and Senate over how the final version of the bill would look. Abbott has already said he intends to sign the bill, a notable difference from two years ago when he and the Legislature withheld billions from public schools following a failed attempt to create a private school voucher program. This year, lawmakers vowed to approve vouchers and new public school funding in tandem. The Legislature finalized the education finance package on a 122-13 vote nearly a month after vouchers . The new dollars in HB 2 will allow school districts to begin making a dent in some of their long-standing challenges -- a laundry list of items that includes reversing budget deficits, providing raises to full-time employees and keeping up with rising operational costs. Before the legislation's final passage on Thursday, Rep. James Talarico , D-Austin, raised questions about the bill, underscoring that public schools' dire situation is partly the result of stagnant funding since 2019, the year lawmakers last raised schools' base dollars and passed a. He sought to have Republican Rep. Brad Buckley of Salado, the bill sponsor, answer why the Republican-led Legislature has not passed major school funding legislation since then, including last session when the state had a at its disposal. The House public education chair only had a few moments to answer the question before lawmakers' speaking time expired, but his response instead focused on HB 2's investments in the basic costs of running a school and paying teachers what they deserve. HB 2 also includes funding for an expansion of the Teacher Incentive Allotment, that awards raises to educators who demonstrate that they have improved their students' academic outcomes -- currently about 6% of teachers. “**Texas Legislature approves $8.5 billion boost for public schools after years of stagnant funding,** ” Texas Tribune's **Jaden Edison** – “The Texas House on Thursday gave the final stamp of approval to legislation authorizing roughly $8.5 billion in funding for public schools, sending the bill to Gov. **Greg Abbott’s** desk where it is soon expected to become law.

Final passage of [House Bill 2](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.y1qQg7vX491TJbzrGLYTuEYT0yv_aZw1IceJac_-o0Y-UGIWKkPTFm9Kz5DRdvb_-aYU7NLaOywMgY5yceksY4shW88ol0Lq3V2TMt6hCBtEkDk2kuBbd7iis9d2eJ100crfEathp5UfUHswM-AEIXvnOy7AmOMQ3s1A565qapjtR8elL0oAoGn1NvQehYnNJ_ZGE5US6RTCZIcfNMQkTQKZW58DYwB0SlXjQdaEsaqMjnpVA8DrpdE6O3CKHjGMad5oU0e1ETp87kGHNUylUYeT4LhC-2303PswfR5sT-LR1jTEasfDLuBhpvZH54FCb6TafJQugZBJ91qeejPcxACxU6kJdwhg_Pma4Bgv3oXwQqTZV-TEvzBVzdiQzRwFY0t1APtdwK0KJ578TPHxjKfLP_wm4mhP8V3CsLfcNLo7bOw11oZ_2ib6tmfmCQVavHw5gV_s6_Gs6f3R6IBXD5go9VXg-lAnGhUlPB-UvzWHYLlUY-SM10DBYsTTqIuf/4gx/Vpnxh7TLRO--kS8peOZ_ww/h10/h001.81ozqaMQx_SUFgUTRthwZArck66cL78vcFW_GdQR_9Y), which will give schools additional money for teacher and staff salaries, educator preparation, special education, safety requirements and early childhood learning, comes on the heels of [extensive negotiations](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.xjnMFfva-73dHOne5Rc0eCyDm7YZItPaA-BvJlf4tsDgkvJmbpj7cnSeDCnGdyvLfJYRWQld0ZGRiCl8AKd4kCe4Jfz7Pi7_RuVKBHN1Ac5VKe5KR1W9UfuE3CojdTG7pxJIo9jn02HEVQJBqmpTvyCxFtvXwmtzu7FnXwJz2gC6ECNusVHDKGXwjpxInOuNwMjpDHr5JA1gEb4sDmj8BJGoGDiUQxbge6dvaywsIIZjAjm_tURFiNgHlScPralrFuqHTRS8oAa5yv8QRZdrVBIhjH9JGQ7Y2CoK9daa8QV2CCKGbGawJi_gPXeu4PwQgrrcEGeii_TmXyTfRD3MOKdXGA2ki8Eg_gq8BfNDJ9fDR1zsgUXOe3zgrLUphmTi73T55sE80wwmKp8WXng93qt-6PSsyovpKIF10MwshGJwsD8yyj_eEizScxi91GbXckJ7jdNOoy6Bp8hYC9h6HS0XdCgOXx8xIGBxUVfJuKcqKtpVPrqRs0_72aHzKjgpzNrcGqeaPk7hxgtGXf0W2Q/4gx/Vpnxh7TLRO--kS8peOZ_ww/h11/h001.foHVf3nyAuuiFUBwPQVqiocH9eG-ej3FVdfdA0Oe1_8) between the House and Senate over how the final version of the bill would look.

Abbott has already said he intends to sign the bill, a notable difference from two years ago when he and the Legislature withheld billions from public schools following a failed attempt to create a private school voucher program. The House public education chair only had a few moments to answer the question before lawmakers’ speaking time expired, but his response instead focused on HB 2’s investments in the basic costs of running a school and paying teachers what they deserve.

HB 2 will provide districts with a $55 per-student increase to their base funding — a number short of the $395 per student hike proposed by the House earlier in the session and far less than the roughly $1,300 school officials said they needed to keep up with inflation. That base funding, known as the basic allotment, provides districts the most flexibility to address the range of needs on their campuses, from salaries and maintenance to instructional materials and athletics.

The bill raises educator pay, which represents more than $4 billion of the proposal’s overall funding. To do so, it dictates:

> Teachers with three to four years of experience in school districts with 5,000 or fewer students will receive a $4,000 raise, while those with five or more years of teaching on their resume will earn $8,000.

> Teachers with three to four years of experience in school districts with more than 5,000 students will earn a $2,500 raise, while those with five or more years of experience will receive $5,000.

Become a PAID subscriber for $5/mo or $50/yr | #TXLEGE “Texas Legislature approves $8.5 billion boost for public schools after years of stagnant funding, ” Texas Tribune's Jaden Edison – “The Texas House on Thursday gave the final stamp of approval to legislation authorizing roughly $8.5 billion in funding for public schools, sending the bill to Gov. Greg Abbott’s desk where it is soon expected to become law. Final passage of , which will give schools additional money for teacher and staff salaries, educator preparation, special education, safety requirements and early childhood learning, comes on the heels of between the House and Senate over how the final version of the bill would look. Abbott has already said he intends to sign the bill, a notable difference from two years ago when he and the Legislature withheld billions from public schools following a failed attempt to create a private school voucher program. This year, lawmakers vowed to approve vouchers and new public school funding in tandem. The Legislature finalized the education finance package on a 122-13 vote nearly a month after vouchers . » The new dollars in HB 2 will allow school districts to begin making a dent in some of their long-standing challenges — a laundry list of items that includes reversing budget deficits, providing raises to full-time employees and keeping up with rising operational costs. Before the legislation’s final passage on Thursday, Rep. James Talarico , D-Austin, raised questions about the bill, underscoring that public schools’ dire situation is partly the result of stagnant funding since 2019, the year lawmakers last raised schools’ base dollars and passed a. » He sought to have Republican Rep. Brad Buckley of Salado, the bill sponsor, answer why the Republican-led Legislature has not passed major school funding legislation since then, including last session when the state had a at its disposal. The House public education chair only had a few moments to answer the question before lawmakers’ speaking time expired, but his response instead focused on HB 2’s investments in the basic costs of running a school and paying teachers what they deserve. HB 2 will provide districts with a $55 per-student increase to their base funding — a number short of the $395 per student hike proposed by the House earlier in the session and far less than the roughly $1,300 school officials said they needed to keep up with inflation. That base funding, known as the basic allotment, provides districts the most flexibility to address the range of needs on their campuses, from salaries and maintenance to instructional materials and athletics. The bill raises educator pay, which represents more than $4 billion of the proposal’s overall funding. To do so, it dictates: Teachers with three to four years of experience in school districts with 5,000 or fewer students will receive a $4,000 raise, while those with five or more years of teaching on their resume will earn $8,000. Teachers with three to four years of experience in school districts with more than 5,000 students will earn a $2,500 raise, while those with five or more years of experience will receive $5,000. HB 2 also includes funding for an expansion of the Teacher Incentive Allotment, that awards raises to educators who demonstrate that they have improved their students’ academic outcomes — currently about 6% of teachers. In place of a significant boost to the basic allotment, the bill will give districts $45 per student that they can only use to increase the salaries of school counselors, librarians, nurses and other support staff. The bill also grants schools $106 per student to pay costs associated with transportation, insurance, utilities and hiring retired educators, which has become more common as schools struggle to fill teacher vacancies. Furthermore, the legislation will overhaul Texas’ to account for the individual needs of each student; establish a compensation system for and mentorship programs; set aside money for schools to better identify learning difficulties among the state’s and fund prekindergarten services; and increase the money districts receive for ." | FREE SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE ENDED : As of July 11, 2022, we have moved to a paywall for free subscribers. body:
Peter, here’s what I saw |
---
Peter — Today I conducted a surprise visit to the Eloy Detention Center in Arizona, an immigration detention facility where people, including DACA recipients, are being held in inhumane conditions. As a Member of Congress, I have a right and a duty to conduct oversight over these detention facilities, announced or unannounced. We were able to enter the facility and conduct an oversight tour. I wasn’t granted access to meet with the folks I was hoping to speak to, but was able to talk with some of the women I saw. They detailed horrible conditions — overlooked medical issues, moldy cells, cruel and dehumanizing treatment. I am sickened by the accounts I heard, and these women asked me to share their stories with the public. I will do everything I can to use my power and position to ensure that we uphold the rule of law, including for detained immigrants. This administration is breaking laws left and right, defying Supreme Court orders, and turning our country into a full-blown authoritarian regime. And I’m not going to sit back and watch while they do it — I’m going to fight back and call out the bad conditions. We can and must do better when it comes to our immigration system, and I promise, Peter, I won’t stop fighting to ensure that the United States remains a safe haven for asylum seekers and a place where the American Dream can still be a reality for us all. name: Katie Porter
subject: I know it’s annoying
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Katie Porter for Governor 2026
body:
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=39765%2E3422442%2EOCc9Vn)
Look, Derek, I get it.
It’s annoying when political campaigns keep asking you for money. I get the same emails you do (and not just the ones from our campaign!).
But until we fix our broken campaign finance system, it’s a necessary evil, especially for a campaign like ours that rejects donations from corporations, lobbyists, and Big Pharma, Big Oil, and Big Bank CEOs.
My team and I try to limit the number of emails we send to your inbox, and we also work to write messages that are at least informative, and as often as possible, fun.
**So here’s an explanation of why we set monthly fundraising targets, like our goal of raising $100,000 over email in May.**
Most political spending on voter contact, such as TV and digital ads, happens in the last few months right before the election—but our budgeting happens a year or more in advance. If we aren’t getting donations until the month before the election, we can’t buy as many ads, and we have less flexibility to respond to dirty political attacks.
We design monthly targets to keep our campaign on track for raising the resources we need. It’s a concrete measure of how much voter contact we’ll be able to do. We push so hard to meet our goals, because we want to run a campaign that speaks to as many voters as possible.
**[Derek, that’s why I’m asking you to chip in $5 today—because it actually matters.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_kp_20250529_2_ak?refcode=em20250529-39765&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=39765_3422442_OCc9Vn&akid=39765%2E3422442%2EOCc9Vn) As a single mom raising three teenage kids, I know how important every dollar is for a family, and I never take your donation for granted.**
[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_kp_20250529_2_ak?refcode=em20250529-39765&refcode2=39765_3422442_OCc9Vn&akid=39765%2E3422442%2EOCc9Vn)
Thanks for reading,
Katie

Katie is running to be California’s next governor because California and our country need a leader who will stand up to Trump to lower costs, protect our rights, and combat climate change. **[Donate ›››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4g-em-footer?refcode=em20250529-39765&amounts=&t=3&refcode2=39765_3422442_OCc9Vn&akid=39765%2E3422442%2EOCc9Vn)**

40th NYC Police Commissioner Bernard Kerik
By Illinois Review

Bernard B. Kerik, former New York Police Commissioner and a cherished friend of Illinois Review’s Editor-in-Chief Mark Vargas, passed away on May 29, 2025, after a private battle with illness. He was 69.

Kerik’s life was marked by uncommon courage, fierce patriotism, and an unwavering dedication to public service. For those who knew him personally, like Vargas, his passing is not just a national loss—but a deeply personal one. He was more than a public figure; he was a loyal friend, a trusted confidant, and a man who always showed up when it mattered most.

Kerik rose to national prominence on September 11, 2001. As the 40th Commissioner of the New York Police Department, he rushed to Ground Zero and stood shoulder-to-shoulder with then-Mayor Rudy Giuliani as the second plane struck the South Tower. In the hours and days that followed, he worked tirelessly to coordinate emergency response, offering a calm, commanding presence as New Yorkers grappled with the unthinkable. That image—Kerik walking through smoke and rubble, leading from the front—is etched into America’s memory.

His career in public service spanned more than four decades. A U.S. Army veteran and lifelong law enforcement officer, Kerik’s service earned him more than 100 medals and commendations, including a presidential commendation for heroism from President Ronald Reagan and two Distinguished Service Awards from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. He had rescued victims from burning buildings, survived assassination attempts, and helped bring some of the world’s most dangerous criminals to justice.

subject: The #1 thing you can do today to stop the Hollywood groomers
body:
take it from me as someone who's lived and worked in Hollywood my whole life...

| | |
---
| | Dear Friend, Please -- for the sake of all our families -- take it from me as someone who's lived and worked in Hollywood my whole life... You are absolutely right if you think Hollywood is reaching right into your family living room with "entertainment" that grooms children.You may remember shows with wholesome messages like Father Knows Best, Marcus Welby, M.D., and even Dennis the Menace.But today when children turn on the TV, they see a Drag Queen leading the Pride Parade on _Blue's Clues_...
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zehbrslnqmvo16hb0dlhhdp0i3omggjuh93pu4jo_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1cdh2bs)
---
| | Or Sesame Street using YOUR tax-dollars to normalize same-sex parents and men in dresses.And the result is an upside-down world where children lecture YOU about what you can and cannot say... ...and they try to "educate" YOU about your "old-fashioned" and "mean" ideas.Today you have a very special chance to stop the Hollywood groomers who are turning our children and grandchildren against us and the Godly values we love. [**Today, I'm inviting you to support the very first children’s television show that actively fights back against the groomers in Hollywood AND reinforces the traditional biblical values that made America great.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zubbqu2auti708lumrp9gm2ncvpr010ltc6bfds8_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1cdh2bs) And it’s only possible with the help of grandparents and seniors like you. Introducing:_ Iggy and Mr. Kirk_.This ground-breaking live-action television show captivates children... ...but more importantly, it builds their character at the same time. Imagine a children’s show that leaves your child or grandchild with a greater sense of right and wrong and an understanding of the truth. Courage, honesty, discernment, forgiveness, empathy, all taught through a biblical and traditional lens. Imagine a children’s show that brings families together instead of driving them apart. Now imagine YOU are the one who makes that show possible. **[Because I can’t beat the Hollywood groomers without your help.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z2vs7k6npek3efbo4thmc4opgfaa6hmhsesc82t8_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1cdh2bs)** Millions of families are already watching Season One of _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ on our streaming service BRAVE+, YouTube, and on DVD. And the reviews from parents, grandparents, and kids are incredible. One Mom of three little girls told us: “Our family was struggling through a pretty difficult day. But I turned on _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ and that was exactly what my heart needed as much as theirs.” It’s amazing that your simple response to this letter can make that kind of difference for a family. Each episode costs around $70,000 to produce. I know that’s a lot of money but it’s actually a fraction of what it would cost if we made our show with a major Hollywood studio. And obviously we won’t work through Hollywood. Hollywood has done quite enough already to destroy American culture and hijack our children. We parents, grandparents, and concerned citizens must take over to rebuild a thriving, healthy, GOOD and GODLY culture. [**That’s why I’m asking you to help us finish Season Two of**** _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_****by giving a gift of $35, $50, $100, $250, $500, $1,000 or more to help us reach our fundraising goal of $70,000 per episode.**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zi4t6g0jdukrap7s4nf4otflb1k42r2rprh892p0_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1cdh2bs)**** Whether you can send $35, $25,000, anything in between, or anything higher or lower – please know that gifts of EVERY size are needed and greatly appreciated. As a special “Thank You” for your **[gift of $50 or more](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2ztn23teethtddutq1e1cs9kda353lj0jui816ag0_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1cdh2bs)** , I’ll send you Season One of _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ for your family to enjoy FREE on DVD. And with your [**gift of $100 or more**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z8rcguq09vj6n1fpl898vjb5sacdr8hjrp68dif0_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1cdh2bs), I’ll also send you a copy of my children’s book: Pride Comes Before the Fall which teaches children to be humble before God instead of prideful. I wrote Pride Comes Before the Fall with the great team at BRAVE books – the same God-focused conservative team that’s bringing _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_ to life. Maybe you’ve seen me and other BRAVE Books authors on Fox News, Newsmax, TBN or other media outlets. Unabashed conservatives like Riley Gaines, Lara Trump, Kevin Sorbo, Missy Robertson, Dinesh D’Souza, John Solomon, Jack Posobiec, and so many more have written a BRAVE Book to stop the Hollywood groomers. Supported by you, BRAVE Books gives parents the tools they need to rebuild our families and reclaim America with the Biblical values our country was founded upon. Now I know there are a lot of places you can spend your money in the next ten minutes. **[But I hope you’ll be a part of history by supporting _Iggy and Mr. Kirk_. ](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zhaebincin1cu3u2n72r2hbnh2g44i9mna9vfv18_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1cdh2bs)** Hollywood groomers have destroyed America’s Godly culture. But today we rebuild from the ashes. And it starts by ensuring the most innocent among us are filled with faith and family – not filth. Thank you for joining us in the fight.

Sincerely,

We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.”That may be good for your family – for now.But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of other children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values!**[**I hope you see why I need your help today.**](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zs1anra82a9o47erlh6es5o3gt8bfatnmnk7uh68_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1cdh2bs)** My name is Kirk Cameron. Maybe you recognize me from the 1980’s family sitcom “Growing Pains” or from my work in inspirational movies like “Fireproof” and “Left Behind.”I know firsthand how dangerous it is to be indoctrinated by leftist values. Pride almost took me down as a young actor in Hollywood.But the gospel saved me. I love being an actor, but what’s far more important is being a husband, dad, grandad, and a Christian.When I saw what book publishers and libraries were doing to indoctrinate children with anti-God, anti-family, anti-America messages, I knew I had a duty to take action. So together with a small Christian book publisher aptly named **Brave Books** , I wrote “As You Grow” to teach children how to grow in wisdom through the fruit of the spirit.And then we decided to go one step further and counter those awful “Drag Queen Story Hours” with a wholesome Story Hour of our own. Our idea was to read the classic books you and I grew up with plus new wholesome **Brave Books** that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism.And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn’t like that one bit.>> Over 50 libraries rejected our request to host our Story Hour. >> The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep us out including booking all the event rooms for themselves.>> Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi (that’s original), **Brave Books** was accused of trying to “confuse and demoralize children,” our supporters were described as “bored moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about,” and on and on. I can’t even print most things these radicals said because it’s so vile.In the end we got two libraries to reverse course by reminding them that their censorship violated the Constitution of the United States.And thousands of parents and grandparents brought their little ones to those Story Hours where we pledged allegiance to the flag, sang “God Bless America,” and read wholesome and Godly books.It was incredible.But here’s the greatest part...From there, parents and grandparents started asking **Brave Books** how they could host Story Hours of their own.And that’s how our nationwide “See You at the Library Day” was born. Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at 360 libraries in 45 states.On the same day, we held hundreds of Story Hours to fill children’s hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God.**I went to as many "See You at the Library" events as I could in one day to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots...**...for a very simple mission – to reject the Left’s radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America’s libraries.And this year, our ambitious goal is to expand “See You at the Library Day” to over 1,000 libraries reaching over 100,000 children.The exact date in August will soon be announced. And before then, what we need is you!It’s going to be expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold Story Hours for 100+ children at each library – that's 100,000+ children in all. **[That’s why I hope you’ll give a sponsorship gift of $175, $350, $525 or more today.](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zss4r4tohmseh4l9aqv1iqgfikdvoqk85vf1b6r0_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1cdh2bs)** Your sponsorship gift will be used to send a “Story Hour Kit” to every parent, grandparent, and patriot who’s organizing a “See You at the Library Day” event. The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for the little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items.**Brave Books** is a small Christian company. They don’t have the millions behind them like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA.Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our 1,000 Story Hours to counter the radical leftists who’ve taken control of our libraries. Knowing that, **[**please consider a sponsorship gift of $175.**](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zfq9q9cghtpi6q5m7ckdds6ijmu6b3nvdk5r7tkg_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1cdh2bs)** That’s enough to sponsor one entire “Story Hour Kit” yourself. Singlehandedly, you’ll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome, Godly, and patriotic message. **[Whatever you can give whether it’s $35, $175, or anything higher or lower please get your sponsorship gift in within the next 48 hours so we know how many libraries we can get into this August!](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2ztbgirf5k761c3ccqqi0t0dqa1jra13sleb6q620_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1cdh2bs)**

body:
If you’ve ever read or heard David Horowitz’s work, then you already know: He wasn’t afraid to tell the truth.

| | |
---
| |
---
| | [](https://e.realamericanreporting.com/rd/9z2zvg67qpkhgka0718la8btet58cmjisj0o6foudcg_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1chh2bs)
---
Dear Fellow Conservative,By now you may have heard that David Horowitz passed away recently. **If you’ve ever read or heard David Horowitz’s work, then you already know: He wasn’t afraid to tell the truth.** **[And today, I want to tell you how you can arm yourself with the truth—in David’s own words—and help us keep his legacy alive for generations to come.](https://e.realamericanreporting.com/rd/9z2z6m2clur0ol16jfie4332osseg7b2tvd97l3ob48_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1chh2bs)** You see, David changed the trajectory of the conservative movement. As Charlie Kirk of Turning Point USA put it: **“David didn’t just write. He debated. He showed up. He walked into hostile auditoriums and faced down Marxist professors, Islamist apologists, and race hustlers – armed only with truth, moral clarity, and a sharp tongue.”** Now that David is gone, it’s up to all of us to carry on his fight. And _his_ Freedom Center is doing exactly that. To supercharge our efforts, to arm you with the truth, and most especially to honor his legacy, today [**I want to send you a copy of the book that changed everything:** **Radical Son: A Generational Odyssey.**](https://e.realamericanreporting.com/rd/9z2zncdtbp946963tbfpjj8fjonc4digoodcjag3tsg_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1chh2bs)
---
| | This is David’s story — from his Marxist upbringing...To his friendship with Huey Newton of the Black Panthers...To the brutal murder that shattered his illusions and opened his eyes to the radical Left’s true nature. Many conservatives call this book _monumental,_ _formative,_ and _one of the most important books a conservative American could ever read._ [**That’s why I want to give you a copy.****All I ask is that you help us keep David’s mission alive by making a tax-deductible donation of $60 or more.**](https://e.realamericanreporting.com/rd/9z2zqsirbag8kpqvi9gdvhv4oh62v73fr1f22pu5fhg_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1chh2bs)
---
| [](https://e.realamericanreporting.com/rd/9z2zmran98no90p0bq56pv93e2v9avkubq2hre6f3bo_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1chh2bs)
---
| | [ **CLAIM YOUR COPY** ](https://e.realamericanreporting.com/rd/9z2zbgi4cok7cnk6vqqnohjlfscvdvo7tacagubt5f0_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1chh2bs)
---
If you can give $100 or more, I’ll send you two copies — one for you, and one to give as a gift to someone who needs to hear David’s warning. Friend, my name is Daniel Greenfield and I am the new CEO of the David Horowitz Freedom Center.It was the honor of my life to work so closely with David for years, fighting for his most critical legacy, the David Horowitz Freedom Center. David used to say that his Freedom Center “isn’t a think tank; it’s a battle tank.” And with the help of patriots like you, over the decades this battle tank has become powerful weapon against the left.**But my friend, your support today is critical if we’re going to keep fighting David’s battle—because the radical Left isn’t backing down.** In fact, mere days after David’s passing, the liberal media took to disrespectful smears of his life’s work.A columnist at the _New York Times_ sneered that David “executed a dizzying transit from the extreme left to the extreme right.” And the _Los Angeles Times_ mocked him as a “raspy-voiced provocateur” who relied on “straw man arguments so much that I’m sure the Scarecrow from _The Wizard of Oz_ is wondering where his royalties are.”**Attacks like these are why the Freedom Center’s battle is far from over.** We must take up the torch of David Horowitz’s legacy and continue his fight because the radical Left is only growing more emboldened and more powerful.They encourage college students to violently protest on behalf of murderous Hamas terrorists...They defend criminals who have no respect for our nation’s laws and blame their illegal behavior on “racism”... They scream from the rooftops that we all must accept “transgender” predators and rapists for the sake of “inclusion”...**David saw it all coming. Decades ago.** **[You’ll get an insider look into his realization as you read _Radical Son._](https://e.realamericanreporting.com/rd/9z2zil6ch5gurb2rbh4bdprqpjgu2frrqp5v59d3i40_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1chh2bs)** As David understood, the radical Left is following the same march to Communism that the former Soviet Union did. And I truly believe it’s only because of David’s work that the modern-day conservative movement is finally fighting the right battle.This isn’t a misunderstanding. This isn’t a disagreement.**This is about stopping the radical Left from DESTROYING AMERICA.** Most conservatives are too scared or too weak to say it. But the Freedom Center isn’t:**Leftists are the extremists. They’re the traitors. They’re the insurrectionists.** The Freedom Center has been at the forefront of this battle — long before the rest of the conservative movement caught on to what the radical Left is doing to our country.And because of how effective we’ve been, we’ve paid the price:
---
* Vimeo and YouTube censored and blocked us from uploading our videos to their websites.
* Left-wing extremists at the Southern Poverty Law Center convinced MasterCard to shut off our credit card processing (thank goodness it’s back on now)...
* Long-time business partners and venues cut our contracts out of the blue.

---
**But we’ve survived because of brave patriotic Americans who stood with us.** People who _know_ what David stood for.
People who _believe_ in the mission.
People who are ready to keep fighting — even now. **[And if I’m describing YOU, then I hope you’ll stand with us today by making a tax-deductible donation of $60 or more.](https://e.realamericanreporting.com/rd/9z2zafjd54qf5u649b8m3r4458k9ekv2a0dtovksmdg_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1chh2bs)** And if you can send back an extra-generous renewal donation of $100 or more, I will send you _two_ copies of this book – one for you, and one for you to give as a gift.This book has changed the face of our conservative movement. So perhaps you have a child, grandchild, friend, or neighbor you could give your second copy to. I truly believe that David’s story is going to continue to change lives – and fuel the fire of our conservative movement for decades to come.That’s exactly what we’re focusing on at the Freedom Center.We have never been more determined to expose the radical Left...Untangle their dark web of money... Upend their propaganda and lies...**And smash their plot to destroy our country.** David’s legacy must be fought for. The Freedom Center is taking up his torch. **[But I need your help to keep his fight going.](https://e.realamericanreporting.com/rd/9z2z6h5vt3ik53hgh2k38qk17kepl0bgpee6ta3jk38_rp22sh2s8i6eob0slie9oj1chh2bs)** Thank you in advance for standing with us.
---
For freedom,
---
**Daniel Greenfield** CEO, David Horowitz Freedom Center

## Trump Tariffs in Legal Limbo
A federal appeals court [lifted one of two rulings](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOqzAQheGnMR2RGRsDhYvb0OW2WyLHjGFWA0Z4kihvv8ruvsHWv_RJ53xcp2sgpn35Hzb0kvK047MwiuA5STgppUI74xKYabtl5LzPOIGGttZtbfQ0B-LXZKvZJ0RAU6FvOtu3w-Csq1ZvLTgz9E6Da9ouutTcUorRYtc3OjahIv_WdGt0o3UH9uLC4IyZte1djKm3ymqcSfJ5-cy0y4qJX_mB5yXmrWK_ihxFmX8KRgWjrLgS87spGE9c7hyE8q5gjPl-Sn0LIoxFwdgasK3RdTgODFzqn86UpNS_0xWM1enn40nMVFynrF62QN98JX_66-HhKwAA__9YwH7G) blocking President Trump’s tariffs on Thursday, just hours after a lower court had rejected the administration’s legal defense. Many of Trump’s tariffs remain blocked under a second, separate ruling from a federal judge, though that judge gave the White House two weeks to appeal before it goes into effect. On Wednesday, the Court of International Trade ruled that Trump [didn’t have the emergency authority](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFvgzAQBeBfY7Ygx2cMHjx0YUvXjsjYZ3LpgSNjhebfV_QvdHvSkz7pva_bdPPEtC2ffkVXU542PHbGWrFM1RdKaaeNcfHMtM4ZOW8RJyVVd5HdBeQUPfF70k10CVEhNOiuvR46a402zd310Gvrg5pNpy2okMBqQIAU5n7QEhpypyY7kFcpe6Vb460BiFIPJoQ0aKElRqq5tI9MW71j4nd-YWlDXht291qfu4APoUahxuM42nkOZyfUeI4RavSlUmA8Yxh-lviw328suSkuPg9ipt30Qstl9cR_av3XFS-nfgMAAP__7olx0Q) he had used to impose tariffs around the world. That was the ruling temporarily overturned Thursday by the appeals court. The contradictory back-and-forth decisions left nations around the world uncertain about the status of the next round of tariffs. The administration said it may [appeal the issue](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZCCPsQ0EDi4hm0svRMZuhj617ZHpGTR_v2K1f7BJJSW9Ur1_9-XukTA__voEjreyZDgPAmaoC_uK23ZgJnh4IkxrASo5wqKkMq00bS-X6JE-i26i2wAU9A2426BHM01W22Z3Rg_SjmuEDcwAsTcgJxmNnXQIKsa1QXfRpOnlTcpB6c76yfZ9lHq0IWyjFlpCRC61-18w8w4bfcobahdKasjtzM9D9H-EmoWaz_PsQl7DVQo1X2ihZnmFmoSaub7Ssw3lVbnFzFCzZyzZU8vVR2h_PrcJiaB2OydqqovPE4nwsIPQ8pE80vc4_8rY26mvAAAA__-aFX_O) to the Supreme Court as early as today.
## Israel Agrees to Ceasefire While Hamas Ponders
Israel has signed off on a 60-day ceasefire proposal from the U.S., and now both countries are [waiting for Hamas leaders to respond.](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAURb8GOwwCohYU29jNtlsaxIe-zVMMMGNmv37j_sJ2N7nJvTnn6zE9HBIe66fbwZYQpwOuTFAKpKm4hCFkPAhWR4T7HIHiscAkhWy5aLkS0-KQ3pOuFhsAJKgKbNPpvh0Go0212UZ1Zm7BDN5oM_R6FkOrm6aXvep8I0OF9l4TrRKNEJ3UtXGDUWoRujfeh14zLWDBElP9HfEoGwR6xxek2se9IruVcmamPpgcmRyv66r9nG-Ku2dyvCOTI-bkgPjmdpe5B5chYAKeIJ_xyMBX9-N4Sc_95NeGBfgWnxmYHKtkl_NCIsymY1qsu0P6-y7_Evay8jcAAP__9lCADw) The proposal includes a two-month ceasefire as well as a plan for Hamas to release 10 living hostages and the remains of 18 dead hostages. Hamas was reported to be seeking changes in the agreement, in particular seeking a guaranteed path from [a temporary ceasefire to a permanent end](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupCAUQL9GuztBQBwLim3s3rZbGpSL3s0VJoBD5u83b3_h9SfnJOfP1_rliCkev92Ftoa0RmyFsVbMa3WZQigUGQ_HTNeWkFP0uEohRxAjKLF6R_xZde9tQJSoerTDpJ_jPBtt-tPKUfvRhD1sSqAcxkkItxmvt8lvOA-qJ_ttE6MSgxCT1A_jZqOUF_pp9j08dacFeqopP_4mivXEwJ_0xvzY09WzPWt9lU796uTSyaW19qh0YUmBSnbI31Qnl4gN7gIeHUO6K1NEaOlmDwURBgFMb4QzleoOLBAyogcjwLsP1HzvCOlVKUWoCTKW-0JoLndy6bP1r0bMVMzUaXFcjv5H-_qjn28r_wUAAP__b4SMAQ) of the war. Israeli hawks have come out against the proposal, saying Israel is now in a position to defeat Hamas entirely and shouldn’t stop.
## Last Grandson of 1840s U.S. President Dies
Harrison Ruffin Tyler, [the last living grandson of 10th U.S. President](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ8GMpD_hwkcXEI2l16IjLsNPTL2yPYNmrdfsdI-wWat_lRVqvr3WB6OIqXtrzvQtpCXhGeN2BqWpblCIVRKETcXIx1rxpgT4CKY0APTg2QLOIqfRfVgA6JA2aPlNzXp-90o0-9WaK74Ch745AMHzhisblVSr15pD6Yne7kxLRln7CbUaNzdSAlMTcb7MKlOMQRquYzPTKntGOInv7GMPh99tHtrr9rJP52YOzGf5zn6tV4tLt6J-To7Me-uFKo5DeV_CJSG9olYhq24BNf3VbASYGrDM-8_FAgvaV8svE6Kkaq5dYpth6P4nd5-Ndnbiq8AAAD__7obgp0) John Tyler, has died at 96, the end of a link back to the distant American past.

John Tyler served as president from 1841 to 1845, a vice president who became president when William Henry Harrison died three weeks after his inauguration. Tyler left office a year before the Mexican-American War began in 1846. How did a president born in 1790 have a grandson who lived until 2025? Harrison Ruffin Tyler’s father was 75 when Harrison was born, and his grandfather, President Tyler, was 63 when Harrison’s dad was born. That means [three generations were able to span 235 years](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpiAUhZ8Gu_sHAVELim3sZtstDSsXvRMEA3fmj2-_cV9hmtOc5Ms535-P9cNTorz_9ic6jmXN-G4JmbGu7CvF2Cgn3H1KdP4tmEoOuCqpBpADaLkGT-leTRdcRFSoO3T9aKZhnq2x3eE2G0OY0OM4hlEbjNu2hcmrXvYjDtp35B6aHLTspRyVeVk_W62DNJPdtjgZYSQG4lJfn4UyHxjTXb6xvrZydskdzFcT-pdQi1BLvq_S-KmEWh6wUIt8Qk1CLV8Nnn9CLVfFRgEzw2c5MvCdsDbYq8-hlQyBsIFnmC30k4QbfW3gI2OFAyFhZHgfxAhH-Woo1NJVF643pUTNjsLI_fSU_i_kH2n9dupfAAAA___muov5).

## Severe Storms Hit Austin
Heavy rains and strong winds caused flash floods and damaged power lines Wednesday night in Austin, [killing one person](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L-O4yAQx_GnwR3R8MfEFBTXuNtrr7TGMN6gJSGCSbx--1PSnK7edj7SV6Pfn4_lA3PJt8_feKXA31tdbrT3QszUlv0oaa81xXpUJmTG-IW3tOVFgx4ljNLAkjCXY7FDCiskrwYK6mwnB9qDHi7BOQNT3M5JJ7V5ih6TXRGtN6OZCKYhh1cMRgNKgbJw8isBgF6TowSklLBAKXNtJ74Q0zf2rRz1Se0U63Uo4cJ878L8EnoWet73_fT1fNALhZ6xcY6FXkDIF2pCz52e1Ej-O-Cjc77Jd1v-r_Le6vXOXTbqj0hd6Fk7L_U4ErhVSUMGpE3eyzXiWSJOziqwdvNmaCHd91xK7u4sLHxeMZf3z_yzpZ9B_w0AAP__ip6Scg) and knocking out power to over 70,000 people. Emergency personnel performed nine water rescues during the storm. [Debris was scattered](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGPozAQBeBfYzpH48GQUFBcQ7fXXonGzDhYGfAKe8Pm35-yf2HrJ3167_37mD8oadrvf2mTsX7HPO9yFpVa5ZjPl_KZMy_5latQrbQ8aOeYZgTsLHS2hZkp6Wv2DY8BeHCNjO7qbz3gANisI7jeuwW8XIMP1867oe0GDzEi3JhvrknjG4OuBefAebgMQQAAA_fCIM4ZD8Kp5uNSV6nyTSXqKz_luCx5a3Rca_0spv1jcDI4ned5eTy_5B0anOioaVExOL13GZw0L6QGpx_Iat7vaz72YgMVCaRqSyVOX5tl2ugubEvNx1Ysp7KsNpI-DE7YD9a70Pm2D5Y5iPUc0Q63obPgYuwJCCC45hj580yqqfRX4-G-UdKf2vV3Zz9H_B8AAP__5FqSgg) on the Texas Longhorns baseball field, and a [window pane fell](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1ygzAQRk8jOpjV8iNTqEhD57QpmQUttiYCedDGMrfP4Bwh_Zv3zfe-ruOVfPDb7ZNWtvJa4rhxToFFeB_zEVyO0c3xiMIkQvM3bW7xIwK2JbRlDaMjH46xKZydwPW6YKtNc-kAe8DibhF6wouZsOvapZ-RzYUZusm0um5a0xfenjJoa9AadANVPzEA4OQ6dsBaqwbYeYl7JXcWflFawhGfvFdzXItg7yKPpOoPhYPCIedcLfFl6CeJ305E4XB-UjgkfvLOZZK4r6l0tNKNyz-wfIuL3bpH9iH41BnVwG0lH94z8r84T4u_AQAA__95OXpR) onto the railing of the State Capitol rotunda. Over 30,000 people were affected by power outages Thursday morning, and Austin Energy said it [might take several days](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMlC7MXAOHFxCNpdeiBrcDNYajEzPePj7FfsLm5VUpVLV-_8YH-SD35__aGMrnyWOO-czsAinMV_B5RjdHK8oTCI0f9HuFj8iYFtBWzUwOvLhGnXp7ATOqJKt6vWfDtAAlqtF0y_Mrel1Y1oATZPuGoO666dmVo5Lb-8yaBtQCpSG2kwMADi5jh2wUoUGdl5iqmVl4Q-dS7jim1M9x60MdhU5zqL5W-BQ4JBzrrfrpJ12ibuPd6jA4X51u0yycipwoCR-Dnyr1yl-r46YOVXxJfTk6nU4Eq4QmhZMj_WxHmWy7sg-BH92faHhuZEPPxPkd-DeFr8DAAD__wGegyE) to restore all connections. In 2015, at least 12 people died, and over 2,000 homes were destroyed. In 1981, floods killed 13 people and caused more than $35 million in damages.

body:
The Establishment never fails to disappoint

| | | | |
---
Friend, I know you’re probably just as fed up with the Republican Establishment as I am.
## **[I hear you loud and clear.](https://go.vbtrb.com/r/ayr0/?__vbtrk=MjkzMzA5OjEwMjk5MDQwNjpuZXdzbGV0dGVy&_uax=MjkzMzA5OjEwMjk5MDQwNg&ct)**
But please hear me out, I’m reaching out as we approach our critical end-of-month fundraising deadline.
You want the GOP majority in Congress to do MORE - **to** **pass the DOGE cuts** ,**codify President Trump’s executive orders** ,**and truly put America First**. I’m with you, and I’m fighting every day to make that happen!

With all the attacks and rollbacks coming out of Washington lately—and with a disastrous budget bill under consideration in the Senate—having effective leadership from our state elected officials to fight climate change and expand renewable energy is more critical than ever.

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 5/30/2025
body:
Police Chief Todd Chamberlain’s first 8 months bring sharp drop in Aurora crime
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Happy Friday,
🎧 Prefer to listen to your news? The **Mountain Minute Podcast** delivers sharp, unfiltered headlines from Colorado and beyond—in just _3 minutes_. Catch even faster takes _(90 seconds or less)_ on our social channels. Listen to today's episode [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)!
Now let's dive in! Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Aurora’s new police chief is [drawing praise](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) after homicides dropped 27% and auto thefts nearly 50% in just eight months. In Colorado Springs, questions persist over Mayor Yemi Mobolade’s role in a false report case, despite the [DOJ declining to indict](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Denver Public Schools is under fire for using lease-purchase financing to build new facilities [without voter approval](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
Meanwhile, Western Slope ranchers are outraged after a [wave of wolf attacks](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), accusing CPW of breaking promises to notify them. A new lawsuit from XX-XY Athletics is [challenging HB25-1312](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) on constitutional grounds. And in Fort Morgan, Memorial Day was honored with full ceremony [despite a grounded flyover](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—proving that tribute doesn’t require spectacle.
🇺🇸 **On the National Stage...** Elon Musk [announced his exit](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) from the federal DOGE initiative after saving taxpayers $175 billion, thanking Trump and vowing the mission would continue. Meanwhile, Byron York argues Musk’s [renewed focus on Mars](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) is a bold move that outpaces Washington’s lunar ambitions.
🗣️ **Commentary Spotlight...** An RMV columnist argues that while President Biden deserves personal compassion amid his cancer diagnosis, the American people deserve answers about the apparent [cover-up of his condition](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
This is the Mountain Minute for Friday, May 30, 2025.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Police Chief Todd Chamberlain’s first 8 months bring sharp drop in Aurora crime](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
The City of Aurora is seeing a significant drop in crime in 2025, a shift that many attribute to the leadership of Police Chief Todd Chamberlain. Since his appointment on September 9, 2024, Chamberlain has implemented a series of reforms aimed at targeting violent crime and increasing public trust.
Property crimes have fallen by 25% year-to-date as of May 18, according to an announcement on the Aurora Police Department’s X account.
The drop includes a 38.5% reduction in motor vehicle theft, 31% in burglary and nearly 16% in larceny. Monthly crime data from the Aurora Transparency Portal shows an average of 871 incidents per month in 2025, down from 1,260 during the same period in 2024.
The latest data suggests crime is falling not just in Aurora, but nationwide. The Major Cities Chiefs Association found a 14% drop in violent crime across 68 cities in early 2025, including a 36% drop in homicides.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

[GET YOUR TICKET HERE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[Free speech fight hits Colorado: XX-XY Athletics sues over HB25-1312](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [FOX NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* XX-XY Athletics is suing Colorado over HB25-1312, a law that redefines gender expression and expands anti-discrimination rules to include chosen names and pronouns.
* The brand argues the law censors its ability to use biologically accurate language in advertising, claiming it violates their free speech rights.
* Founder Jennifer Sey says the law forces businesses to promote an ideology that contradicts truth, calling it a direct attack on liberty and expression.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---

The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[Multiple wolf attacks hit Western Slope ranchers—CPW accused of broken promises](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Ranchers in Pitkin County suffered multiple wolf attacks over Memorial Day weekend, with calves killed or severely injured across three ranches.
* Colorado Parks and Wildlife (CPW) is under fire for allegedly failing to alert ranchers when collared wolves from the Copper Creek pack entered livestock areas.
* A CPW-employed range rider was mistakenly dispatched to the wrong land, highlighting communication failures and eroding ranchers' trust in the wolf reintroduction program.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
** ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[Garbo: Biden deserves compassion—but who lied to keep control?](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY C. J. GARBO****| COMMENTARY | MAY 29** _First, let’s say what should be said: cancer is brutal. No matter the person or politics, a diagnosis of aggressive, metastatic prostate cancer is devastating. President Biden is a husband, a father, and a human being._
__
**[Flyover grounded, but Fort Morgan keeps faith with the fallen](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY HARVEY BAKER, NE CO | LOCAL | MAY 29** _Cloudy skies didn’t stop more than 400 people from gathering at Riverside Cemetery on Saturday for Fort Morgan’s Memorial Day ceremony. Organized by American Legion Post 19 and joined by the 140th Fighter Squadron from Buckley Space Force Base, the event honored fallen service members._
__
**[Two CVRs, one pattern: Arapahoe County rewrote its election record, critics say–and no one’s accountable](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | MAY 27** _Arapahoe County quietly replaced its 2020 general election cast vote record (CVR) in early 2025 – years after the election was certified. The change came without public notice, audit, or oversight. The reason? A Yale professor raised concerns about a strange pattern in the data._
__

| | Fellow Conservative, What an incredible month. Things are moving fast in Washington and we're making history.

**President Trump and our Republican majorities are ALL IN to finally rein in and reform our out-of-control federal government... and we can 't let up for a moment!**

Help us keep up our conservative fight for America's future. We need your support as we battle back against the left's lawfare and obstructionism and work to defeat the National Democrats at the ballot box to protect our hard-won majorities.** **[**_HELP US REACH OUR MAY GRASSROOTS FUNDRAISING GOAL >>>_**](http://trk.tedcruz.)

I'm working hard on several critical priorities, and we saw a lot of action this month:

The **Take It Down Act** , which I introduced in the Senate, was passed by Congress and signed into law by President Trump.**** We're forcing online platforms to remove nonconsensual intimate imagery within 48 hours of a request from a victim, and we've made the distribution of such images a crime punishable by fines or jail time.

The **REINS Act** , now included in the House budget bill, would prevent major regulations - anything with a compliance price tag of more than $100 million - from taking effect without being passed by Congress and signed into law by the President of the United States. The REINS Act will finally restore constitutional balance and halt bureaucratic overreach.

The **Invest America Act** , another piece of legislation I authored, was also included in the House budget bill. It would create private investment accounts for every American child, seeded with $1,000 when they are a newborn. When these children turn 18, they will have a resource to put to work to pursue higher education, start a business, or buy a home. If it becomes law, it will be one of our Republican Party's landmark achievements.

**I also called out National Public Radio in a big way** , after President Trump issued an executive order to cut off their public funding - the time is long overdue for real accountability for these far-left propagandists posing as journalists.

And when **I grilled representatives from America 's major sports leagues** earlier this month, I left them knowing that fans are growing extremely frustrated with their streaming practices and for good reason. It can be next to impossible to find some games at all and many games that used to be free or easy to find are now spread across pricey apps and exclusive deals.

Our May end-of-month fundraising deadline is coming up fast at midnight tomorrow.

We can't afford to fall short of our goal as we keep charging forward to get big things done!

[**Thank you so much for any contribution you can send**](http://trk.tedcruz.-sWs_6T_z9Udw)**** to help us roll into the summer months strong.

For Liberty,

Ted Cruz **PS:** The Democrats are gearing up to roll back everything we are doing to Save America and to reverse the terrible damage that was done during the Biden administration- we _MUST_ be prepared for their attacks, which is why we still need YOUR help so urgently. **[Please consider making a donation of $5, $10, or $20 right now to fuel our fight...](http://trk.tedcruz.) **

I wanted to be a doctor, but I soon realized our politics were making us sick. My dad came to Detroit from Egypt in 1978, chasing the American dream in the state that built it — a promise that if you worked hard, you’d get a fair shot. That’s the dream that raised me. That’s the dream this country is supposed to be about. But the illnesses of corporate greed and political corruption are killing that dream. Now, we have an opportunity to take on the billionaires, the broken system, and the politicians who shill for them. We’re going to fight like hell to make sure every family, not just the billionaires and oligarchs, can achieve the American dream. This campaign isn’t just about winning a Senate seat, Peter. It’s about taking back our democracy — from the monopolies jacking up your grocery bill to the politicians who do their bidding behind closed doors. We’re building something real. For working people. And savvy grassroots activists like you know, just like we do, that we can’t stop watching the people we help elect: after the elections, we have to keep organizing support for the policies we like and pushing back against the ones we don’t. When the public tunes out between elections and the only people our elected officials hear from are the paid lobbyists of wealthy corporations, our government stops being accountable to the needs of ordinary families. Democracy never sleeps, and neither can we. So we ask that you support our work, so we can continue to engage in this fight every moment of every day. So our kids grow up in democracy, not dystopia. Thank you for your support for all we do! — You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. Dear Friend, Summer is almost here. Most state lawmakers are out of session, but our state freedom caucuses are still hard at work. All day, every day to defend your liberties. Here's the latest:
---
|
---
**LOUISIANA** If you’ve ever driven down the interstate in Louisiana, you’ve probably noticed a billboard for a trial lawyer every mile or so. There’s a reason for that — Louisiana has one of the most lawsuit-happy legal climates in the country. It’s a system that’s been criticized for encouraging frivolous lawsuits and making trial lawyers rich at everyone else’s expense.But the **Louisiana Freedom Caucus** is working to change that. And this week, they made a big move in the right direction. Rep. Emily Chenevert, a proud LAFC member, sponsored a bill — backed by the entire LA Freedom Caucus — that cracks down on lawsuit abuse by stopping people who are mostly at fault from filing a lawsuit to seek damages. The legislation pushes for more personal responsibility and is expected to help bring down sky-high insurance rates for families across the state. **Both chambers passed the bill.** Now, it’s up to Governor Jeff Landry. Even though he’s a Republican, it’s not clear whether he’ll sign the bill or not. We’ll be watching — and we’ll keep you posted.

Stephen Frank, on his TV show last week. Click on the image below to hear Stephen's answer.

[](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjn-2BF3Ka3pedtTI7Xx70G-2Fk3Gxpoh-2BXs4UjUUauyAumfvG0qNuPVi4StXSsxO-2FJVfsg-3D-3DC-Eo_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHer4yYMTpz9znLMs0BjOelnc8y7WHWXUDi5HnJE61vst4lr4AXmlVfp4Rsi3tMUscvFqfRfkvsOrTUqNQnO7IF660YUDYf-2FAlbiVjsQe8RSYYLsXpVp69x-2FiKdKLAQMB9fe5azBYisN-2FMpiGjKcQVLbr-2BdH2-2FZIFFUA0HLyI-2B8Sbp5VVBVbceLI3RRNUp7HU7Z0UzmbwwU33IykoJma9VwV2yhgIgnFi5Bf2QRPZJt1Hw0-3D)
---
|
---
**MISSOURI** We have a big fight brewing in the Show Me State. The "Republican" Governor Mike Kehoe just called for a June 2 special session to pass a bill doling out massive subsidies to the Kansas City Royals and the Kansas City Chiefs. The governor wants taxpayers to hand out millions to the billionaire owners of these two professional sports teams so that they don't move...get this...10 miles to the west across the state border into Kansas. The **Missouri Freedom Caucus** put out a statement laying down their position. If it's a standalone bill, they will vote NO and use all procedural tools (like the filibuster) at their disposal to stop it. Or they can be compelled to support it if leadership includes huge, GOP priorities like broad-based tax reform. Read their release here:

clean_body: | | | | Dear Friend, Summer is almost here. Most state lawmakers are out of session, but our state freedom caucuses are still hard at work. All day, every day to defend your liberties. Here's the latest: | LOUISIANA If you’ve ever driven down the interstate in Louisiana, you’ve probably noticed a billboard for a trial lawyer every mile or so. There’s a reason for that — Louisiana has one of the most lawsuit-happy legal climates in the country. It’s a system that’s been criticized for encouraging frivolous lawsuits and making trial lawyers rich at everyone else’s expense.But the Louisiana Freedom Caucus is working to change that. And this week, they made a big move in the right direction. Rep. Emily Chenevert, a proud LAFC member, sponsored a bill — backed by the entire LA Freedom Caucus — that cracks down on lawsuit abuse by stopping people who are mostly at fault from filing a lawsuit to seek damages. The legislation pushes for more personal responsibility and is expected to help bring down sky-high insurance rates for families across the state. Both chambers passed the bill. Now, it’s up to Governor Jeff Landry. Even though he’s a Republican, it’s not clear whether he’ll sign the bill or not. We’ll be watching — and we’ll keep you posted. | THE MATT GAETZ SHOW How important are the state freedom caucuses at fighting the special interest lobbyists in the state capitols?That's the question former Congressman Matt Gaetz posed to SC Freedom Caucus member, Rep. Stephen Frank, on his TV show last week. Click on the image below to hear Stephen's answer. | MISSOURI We have a big fight brewing in the Show Me State. The "Republican" Governor Mike Kehoe just called for a June 2 special session to pass a bill doling out massive subsidies to the Kansas City Royals and the Kansas City Chiefs. The governor wants taxpayers to hand out millions to the billionaire owners of these two professional sports teams so that they don't move...get this...10 miles to the west across the state border into Kansas. The Missouri Freedom Caucus put out a statement laying down their position. If it's a standalone bill, they will vote NO and use all procedural tools (like the filibuster) at their disposal to stop it. Or they can be compelled to support it if leadership includes huge, GOP priorities like broad-based tax reform. Read their release here: | Summer is a critical season in our fight to defend liberty, uphold the Constitution, and preserve the conservative values that make our nation strong. The battles ahead require resources—and your generosity ensures we can continue to speak boldly, equip citizens, and stand firm against the growing threats to our freedoms. Will you help us protect liberty this summer? Your donation directly fuels our mission to promote limited government, free markets, and individual responsibility. Every gift—large or small—makes a real impact. We'll be back with another update next week. Until then, please be sure to our efforts so that we can support our State Freedom Caucuses!In Liberty, Andy RothPresident State Freedom Caucus Network |
