**Alarming fact: More than 48 million Americans hear so poorly that their quality of life significantly suffers as a result.**

The problem: Most wait too long to act, hoping their hearing will improve on its own. Sadly, it never does.

But now, **a game-changing device is revolutionizing the hearing aid industry,** and experts say it's the biggest breakthrough they've seen in over a decade.

It's hear.com's **new IX hearing aid.**

And it’s the perfect solution at the perfect time—when more and more people are eager to maintain their quality of life and overcome these limitations.

It’s no wonder **hear.com's IX hearing aid has taken the U.S. by storm since its release earlier this year** offering hope and unprecedented clarity to thousands across America.
[Check if you qualify](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2za58nfgp3vv6pmsc44nh3stetlrqpp7413rk4ito_rp22sh2s8i6eob0sdh66oj6cdh2bs)
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zbjf4ia2ao9m50snrh9l6ua02mj9nehs9pjbg8gg_rp22sh2s8i6eob0sdh66oj6cdh2bs)
What makes hear.com’s IX hearing aid so special?

It’s one of **the world’s first hearing aids with dual processing.**

This is special because it’s the first time engineers have been able to pack not one, but two state-of-the-art computer chips into a device this small.

The result? **An unprecedented amount of power and clarity.**

This means that hear.com’s IX hearing aids offer all of the usual benefits of modern hearing aids—from smartphone connectivity to Bluetooth streaming—with the added bonus of something completely new: they can process speech and background noise independently, then recombine them for **unparalleled, crystal clear sound.**

“It's not just about volume,” explains hear.com founder Paul Crusius. “It's about speech clarity. And that's precisely what IX is designed to optimize.”

In other words: **with double the power comes double the clarity—and all that in a virtually invisible design!**

GOP Senator Ted Cruz **[fired back with facts](https://substack.com/redirect/52b80647-bc0a-4b39-b05d-9db86d2be7c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after Sen. Amy Klobuchar defended activist federal judges who have made it their mission to antagonize President Donald Trump's America First agenda.
**[He did not hold back...](https://substack.com/redirect/52b80647-bc0a-4b39-b05d-9db86d2be7c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/52b80647-bc0a-4b39-b05d-9db86d2be7c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/52b80647-bc0a-4b39-b05d-9db86d2be7c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
"The reason that these judges, who were appointed by Ronald Reagan, yes they still exist, and the Bushes, and judges appointed by Donald Trump have been making these decisions is because this is not legal!" Klobuchar said. "Donald Trump himself has used his social media account, the White House account, posting an image of himself wearing a crown saying 'long live the king!'"
"We do not live in a kingdom and Elon Musk is not his court jester!" she continued. "No one is above the law! That is why 39 different judges,... have made clear that these are illegal actions. And these judges have rightly blocked these actions!"
**[Cruz came out storming when it was his turn to speak](https://substack.com/redirect/52b80647-bc0a-4b39-b05d-9db86d2be7c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , asking a hearing witness how many nationwide injunctions were issued in previous periods versus how many have been issued in the last 2 months.
"Let that sink in!" Cruz said. "There have been more nationwide injunctions against President Trump in the last 2 months than in the entire 20th century!"
**["Democrats today hate democracy!](https://substack.com/redirect/52b80647-bc0a-4b39-b05d-9db86d2be7c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Democrats today are angry at the voters for reelecting Donald Trump,... and they engage in law fare to stop democracy from operating!!" Cruz sounded off.

# Trump GOES OFF on three activist judges
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7a08bc99-f572-48aa-8b51-457dd8a6458e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

President Donald Trump **[unleashed hell on Truth Social at 3 activist judges](https://substack.com/redirect/7a08bc99-f572-48aa-8b51-457dd8a6458e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** who have opposed his tariffs, blocking them in court.
* **Trump posted a furious 500-word attack on the judges who tried blocking his tariff agenda** \- The president questioned where the Court of International Trade judges "come from" and accused them of damaging America out of "hatred of Trump."
* **Trump wrote** \- "The horrific decision stated that I would have to get the approval of Congress for these Tariffs,... In other words, hundreds of politicians would sit around D.C. for weeks, and even months, trying to come to a conclusion as to what to charge other Countries that are treating us unfairly,... If allowed to stand, this would completely destroy Presidential Power -- The Presidency would never be the same!"
* **The president turned on the conservative Federalist Society and Leonard Leo** \- Despite the group helping him pick Supreme Court justices during his first term, Trump called Leo a "real sleazebag" and "bad person" who "probably hates America," alleging Leo controls judges and has his own ambitions, though Leo responded graciously saying he was grateful for Trump's court transformation.

| Friends,

We look forward to seeing you next week in Washington, D.C., for the Special Competitive Studies Project's AI+ Expo. We're excited to announce that With Honor Action will participate in two panels. The panels will both be recorded and will occur on Wednesday, June 4.
---
| [ ](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=5dd421f62a&e=33f53a5b1a)
---
The first panel, from 9:30 to 10:30 AM on the South Stage, will feature With Honor Co-Founder and CEO Rye Barcott and will explore service-oriented leadership and how the veteran leadership of the For Country Caucus remains one of the only bipartisan caucuses remaining in Congress that regularly works together on legislation.
| [ ](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=1389c76132&e=33f53a5b1a)
---
On the second panel from 11:00 to 11:30 AM on the Central Stage, With Honor Action Vice President of Government Affairs Sean McClintock will participate in a fireside chat with Lt. Gen. (Ret.) Michael Groen, who last served as the Commander of the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center, and Charles Correll Jr., highlighting the impact that veterans continue to have on national security policy in Washington D.C. after leaving the military.
| With three full days of programming and an [extensive show floor](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=a38e044c86&e=33f53a5b1a) featuring AI product demos and drone competitions, this year's AI+ Expo promises to be unforgettable.
---
| [Free Registration](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=2f1de523ec&e=33f53a5b1a "Free Registration")
---
|
---
| **Service Member and Veterans' Brain Health**
---
| [ ](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=06359a21aa&e=33f53a5b1a)
---
| Over Memorial Day weekend, CBS re-aired a [story](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=fd8170abab&e=33f53a5b1a) featuring Frank Larkin, the father of Ryan Larkin, who died by suicide in 2017. Since then, Frank has led an extraordinary effort to uncover the hidden scarring in Ryan’s brain—damage not caused by a single traumatic event like a roadside bomb, but by repeated, low-level blasts from the very weapons Ryan used while serving our country.
---
|
---
---
| Last June, With Honor Action facilitated a meeting between Frank, the Jean Perkins Foundation, and the bipartisan veterans of the For Country Caucus—leaders who have seen firsthand the toll traumatic brain injuries take on the warfighter and who understand better than anyone the challenges our veterans face both in and out of uniform. Late last year, we were proud to help pass key provisions of the _Blast Overpressure Safety Act_ , legislation championed by With Honor Action ally and U.S. Army veteran Senator Joni Ernst, and bolsters the Pentagon's oversight of the effects weapons have on service member brain health. This work has already made an impact, as the Department of Defense has already [increased](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=17059d53f4&e=33f53a5b1a) investments in brain health and blast overpressure research and updated its standoff distances for [heavy weaponry](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=89fc2760f5&e=33f53a5b1a).

As I reported on this week, on May 25, 2025, the Israeli military bombed the Fahmi al-Jarjawi School in Gaza City, a shelter for displaced families. At least 36 people were killed, including 18 children and six women--burned alive in the flames. Among the survivors was five-year-old Ward al-Sheikh Khalil, who escaped the flames that claimed her mother and five siblings. This incident highlighted two critical and hard truths: Corporate media continues to whitewash atrocity, and we need to [invest in tools](https://substack.com/redirect/57740c6e-01d7-48d0-8040-75bb6653b990?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to ensure the media we are consuming is accurate and reliable.
**Let 's Address This.**
**Support** _**Let 's Address This**_**as a paid subscriber and let 's continue to build this movement for justice together.**
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..2uN9XjwucGZaWLsW5eYaRO4jfkZB8RqiayvNYrE6c1k?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=164763841)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/55420de3-f2e3-4068-a35b-f70310826b48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Credit: Boston University College of Communication Center for Mobile Communication Studies
Despite the harrowing nature of this event, much of the corporate media coverage was muted. Corporate headlines often echoed the Israeli military's talking points, diminished the seriousness of this atrocity, and in some cases, flat out lied. For example, consider this grotesque headline from The Washington Post:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/93b79e42-cc65-4c2e-99e0-10fe02ec9022?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Who conducted the strikes? How many people were killed? Who was killed? How were they killed? We know none of this vital information from the headline. Worse, the headline sanitizes the atrocity by claiming that food is now being distributed. First, what does this food distribution have to do with deadly strikes? Second, it is an abject lie to claim that food is actually being distributed, as the UN reports that the Israeli blockade is resulting in famine, and moreover, the alleged distribution is but a drop of the food necessary for survival. Meanwhile, just 24 hours later the Washington Post had no problem naming Russia as the aggressor against Ukraine.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2fd0a807-10f5-483f-9fff-41f8f1c7bdd0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And the Washington Post wasn't alone in failing to report meaningful information. Reuters skipped the mass killing of Palestinians altogether, and went straight to misrepresenting the food crisis. The Reuters headline would have us believe that it is looters, not the Israeli government, who is blocking food into Gaza. This misdirection, bias, and flat out disinformation is only further enabling harm and genocide, and doing nothing to keep anyone safe.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/97127aad-e2cc-4aa5-84ae-451df6423f94?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Not to be outdone in misinformation and misdirection, the New York Times ignored the broader story altogether, and spoke of one family only. Instead of acknowledging that Israeli airstrikes on a school turned shelter killed more than 50 people, the New York Times chose to minimize the atrocity. Worse, it then quotes the Israeli government in a sympathetic way as "checking" if it had harmed "uninvolved civilians." First of all, how does the New York Times define an "uninvolved civilian" versus an "involved civilian?" We never find out. Second, why is the New York Times whitewashing the murder of civilians at all? Finally, why did the New York Times refuse to report that the Israeli strike on civilians burned them to death in holocaust style fashion?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f86d72f4-4765-4517-b1df-eba2fcfb0ba3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This pattern of failed and biased reporting raises concerns about media run by billionaires, and their sanitization of atrocities. Meanwhile, several independent outlets effectively highlighted the lack of warning before the horrific strikes by the Israeli government, the absence of militant activity at the school, the killing by burning of babies, Israel's illegal blockade causing famine in Gaza, and the lack of any meaningful accountability for the Israeli government. These reports underscored the importance of diverse media perspectives in understanding complex conflicts.
But while independent media outlets readily provided these more detailed and factually accurate accounts, there remain two problems. One, their reach is just not yet to the level of corporate media platforms backed by billionaires. Two, too few readers yet have easy access to identify accurate vs biased reporting.
## How Do We Address These Problems?
We are living through a moment where babies are being burned alive in Gaza. Where entire families are being incinerated in their sleep. And yet, corporate media headlines still dance around the truth--sanitizing horror, softening genocide, and refusing to name what is plainly before us.
Let me be clear: this is not journalism. This is complicity.
But I don't believe in just naming the problem--I believe in building the solution. Because we are not helpless. And we are absolutely not without tools.
Here are two solutions that work:
### 1\. Support Independent Writing
When I launched _Let 's Address This_, it wasn't just to report on injustice--it was to confront it and build a community to stand against it. Over 400 pieces later, we've reached more than 25 million people. That reach exists _because of you._ Because you've chosen to invest in truth over profit. Because you understand that corporate media can't be trusted to tell the full story--especially when their million-dollar advertisers and billionaire owners demand silence.
If you're a subscriber--thank you. If you're not yet--[join us](https://substack.com/redirect/6e0c7db4-2941-4255-a225-f03c17ec692f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Because while we will _never_ enact a paywall, every share, every read, and every subscription is a blow against the systems that profit off our ignorance.
### 2\. Use Ground News--Right Now
If you care about getting the critical context missing from your typical newsfeeds--and I know you do--you need [Ground News](https://substack.com/redirect/57740c6e-01d7-48d0-8040-75bb6653b990?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I use it every day to write these articles. It's not just a news app and website--it's a weapon against propaganda.
Here's why [Ground News](https://substack.com/redirect/57740c6e-01d7-48d0-8040-75bb6653b990?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) matters:
✅ **Bias Detection** - See immediately where every outlet leans: left, center, or right. No more hidden agendas. No more smoke and mirrors.
✅ **Funding Transparency** - Know who's pulling the strings. Whether it's a defense contractor, a pharmaceutical giant, or a billionaire mogul, Ground News exposes the money behind the media.
✅ **Global Comparison** - Get a 360° view. See how the same story is reported in the U.S., the Middle East, and Europe. Build factual conclusions. Don't let corporate America build them for you.
[Subscribe to Ground News](https://substack.com/redirect/76993d48-bc70-4f7e-b6de-c6a3c10c2f10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
So my ask of you is this: As you navigate media inaccuracies, funding secrecy, and national bias, do so with tools that stop letting other people's agendas control how you think: subscribe to Ground News for 40% off--just $5/month. The below link directly supports my work--and most importantly, it arms you with the ability to verify your sources in an era of relentless disinformation.
And unlike billionaire-run media, Ground News is reader-supported. It is built for people, not profits. It answers to you, not advertisers.
[Subscribe to Ground News](https://substack.com/redirect/76993d48-bc70-4f7e-b6de-c6a3c10c2f10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### **The Time for Action Is Now**
Again, we are not powerless. We can still choose what we read. We can still choose to support the journalists and platforms that put truth over profits. We can still fight back--with information, with solidarity, and with courage. This is why I write. This is why I publish daily. This is why I partner with [Ground News](https://substack.com/redirect/57740c6e-01d7-48d0-8040-75bb6653b990?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Democracy doesn't die overnight--it dies one ignored atrocity at a time. Let us make sure it does not die on our watch.

**Alarming fact: More than 48 million Americans hear so poorly that their quality of life significantly suffers as a result.**

The problem: Most wait too long to act, hoping their hearing will improve on its own. Sadly, it never does.

But now, **a game-changing device is revolutionizing the hearing aid industry,** and experts say it's the biggest breakthrough they've seen in over a decade.

It's [hear.com's](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2z7650n35bs886rkg7s74ihkroivgv1ei6rfi82j8_rp22sh2s8i6eob0sdh61o32chh2bs) **new IX hearing aid.**

And it’s the perfect solution at the perfect time—when more and more people are eager to maintain their quality of life and overcome these limitations.

It’s no wonder **[hear.com's](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2z36okf1enbs4dv1qv7ndri7cmcaldhlevpe3j96o_rp22sh2s8i6eob0sdh61o32chh2bs) IX hearing aid has taken the U.S. by storm since its release earlier this year** offering hope and unprecedented clarity to thousands across America.
[Check if you qualify](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2z2143bnilk3rckjogkj3jkkt9v5q3qah7135cec8_rp22sh2s8i6eob0sdh61o32chh2bs)
[](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zkt34kenlfcua4nork87q45u68setv0sad8g36ug_rp22sh2s8i6eob0sdh61o32chh2bs)
What makes [hear.com's](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zucde49ja80voh88ngadu07m9fh65g6kdfgrt778_rp22sh2s8i6eob0sdh61o32chh2bs) IX hearing aid so special?

It’s one of **the world’s first hearing aids with dual processing.**

This is special because it’s the first time engineers have been able to pack not one, but two state-of-the-art computer chips into a device this small.

The result? **An unprecedented amount of power and clarity.**

This means that [hear.com's](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zts2g7iskukl9gspehdht1357jfb2cu4m7mslge0_rp22sh2s8i6eob0sdh61o32chh2bs) IX hearing aids offer all of the usual benefits of modern hearing aids—from smartphone connectivity to Bluetooth streaming—with the added bonus of something completely new: they can process speech and background noise independently, then recombine them for **unparalleled, crystal clear sound.**

“It's not just about volume,” explains [hear.com's](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zv0hnk67ag7tblr3g6b1ciblokend80okci9f7mg_rp22sh2s8i6eob0sdh61o32chh2bs) founder Paul Crusius. “It's about speech clarity. And that's precisely what IX is designed to optimize.”

In other words: **with double the power comes double the clarity—and all that in a virtually invisible design!**

❌ It will roll back clean energy and infrastructure investments, hurting rural communities and setting us back in the fight against the climate crisis
❌ It will further explode our deficit and add trillions to the debt, harming our economic stability and the security of future generations of Americans

The far-Left wants the current administration to obey the dictates of federal district court judges rather than the will of a majority of the American people. But do federal judges control the executive branch? Does the judicial branch have the final say in determining what is or is not constitutional? Because the far-Left has undermined informed patriotism by promoting a distorted view of our nation's history and Constitution--including the judicial branch--many Americans do not know the answers to these questions. That's why your participation in Hillsdale College's is urgently requested. Your response will only take a few minutes, and the survey topic is crucial to the future of liberty and separation of powers in America. You will help Hillsdale College form effective strategies to educate millions of Americans about the separation of powers and checks and balances--including the judiciary's proper role in our government. You can easily complete your National Survey on the U.S. Judicial Branch using this secure link: Thank you for your time and attention--and for joining us in the defense of liberty. Warm regards, Larry P. Arnn President, Hillsdale College Pursuing Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844 | .

Raising Brave Kids in a Wobbly World

with The Mud Hen Mama

Monday, June 16

9amPT/10amMT/11amCT/12pmET

What do a quirky bird with funky toes and a mom of ten have in common? A bold, countercultural mission rooted in truth.

Join us for an inspiring conversation with the founder of Mud Hen Mama (MHM)—a resource hub for families seeking to raise children
with firm, biblical convictions. You’ll hear the heartfelt (and humorous!) origin story behind the name "Mud Hen Mama" and how one
mama’s search for meaning led her to an unlikely symbol of endurance, unity, and faith: the American Coot.

In this webinar, you’ll discover:

* The surprising symbolism of the Mud Hen and why it matters;

* How MHM curates books that support biblical values in a world that often doesn’t;

* Why standing together is key in raising the next generation of truth-bearers; and,

* How you can link arms with other like-minded families through the Mud Hen Mama community.

If you’ve ever felt alone in your efforts to raise godly kids in a culture that pushes back—this is for you. Come be encouraged,
equipped, and reminded that you’re not alone. Together, we endure. --✨

VIRGINIA SUMMIT

FRIDAY, AUGUST 1, 2025
REGENT UNIVERSITY LIBRARY
1000 REGENT UNIVERSITY DRIVE
VIRGINIA BEACH, VA

Virginia Moms for America is inviting you to attend their one-day summit at Regent University in Virginia Beach on Friday, August
1st. Come be encouraged and uplifted by messages of unity, light, and purpose offered by Moms for America’s founder and president,
Kimberly Fletcher, and Lead Cottage Meeting Instructor, Juleen Jackson. Dr. Kelly Kohls, the founder of the National Schoolboard
Leadership Council, will also attend to help concerned parents learn how to get involved with their local schoolboards from
general attendance to running for office.

[] [] Raising Brave Kids in a Wobbly World with The Mud Hen Mama Monday, June 16 9amPT/10amMT/11amCT/12pmET What do a quirky bird with funky toes and a mom of ten have in common? A bold, countercultural mission rooted in truth. Join us for an inspiring conversation with the founder of Mud Hen Mama (MHM)—a resource hub for families seeking to raise children with firm, biblical convictions. In this webinar, you’ll discover: The surprising symbolism of the Mud Hen and why it matters; How MHM curates books that support biblical values in a world that often doesn’t; Why standing together is key in raising the next generation of truth-bearers; and, How you can link arms with other like-minded families through the Mud Hen Mama community. If you’ve ever felt alone in your efforts to raise godly kids in a culture that pushes back—this is for you. Come be encouraged, equipped, and reminded that you’re not alone. Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.

Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. Peter,

Date: May 29, 2025
From: Lauren Groh-Wargo, Fair Fight
Subject: A critical time
Hey friend,
Today, I want to talk to you about why this is a critical time for Fair Fight’s efforts to protect voting freedom.
In the last few election cycles, extremists have made it clear that they are willing to stop at _nothing_ to suppress the vote, even if it means scaring people away from voting and civic engagement altogether.
The far right’s actions are _anti-democratic_ and _designed to target_ marginalized communities — which already face barriers to fair participation and representation.

In the 1990s, thousands of women in Peru—mostly Indigenous, rural, and low-income—were forcibly sterilized under a government policy implemented under former President Alberto Fujimori.

Among them was 34-year-old Celia Ramos, who died in 1997 after undergoing a surgical sterilization she had not validly consented to. This month, the Center for Reproductive Rights and partners Study for the Defense of Women's Rights (DEMUS) and the Center for Justice and International Law (CEJIL), argued Celia's case before the Inter-American Court of Human Rights (IACtHR), marking the first time the Court will hear a case on Peru's forced sterilization policy.

The Center asked the Court to recognize forced sterilization as a form of reproductive and gender-based violence, and to establish reparations for victims like Celia. The case also seeks concrete measures to ensure this abuse never happens again, such as strengthened consent protections in reproductive health care.

"Forced sterilizations were acts of power—and of violence—against the most vulnerable women in Peru," said Catalina Martínez Coral, the Center's Vice President for Latin America and the Caribbean. "Celia Ramos's case presents the Court with the opportunity to set clear standards for States to follow in finally addressing Peru's history of forced sterilization and reproductive violence."

**_Michigan: Court Strikes Down Harmful Restrictions_**

A Michigan court struck down three abortion restrictions, ruling that they violate the state's voter-approved constitutional amendment safeguarding abortion rights. The Center brought this case on behalf of **Northland Family Planning Centers and Medical Students for Choice** , challenging laws that mandated biased "counseling," required patients to wait 24 hours before accessing abortion care, and prohibited qualified clinicians from providing care. Judge Sima Patel agreed that these laws were unconstitutional and rejected the state's argument that they were necessary for patient safety. This is a huge win for evidence-based, patient-centered care.

**_Vermont: A Shield Law Breakthrough_**

In May, Vermont passed VT S.28, a strong expansion of abortion care privacy and shield protections for providers. The Center helped draft and advocate for this bill in collaboration with local providers. The law updates telemedicine policy to allow asynchronous patient-provider relationships and allows prescribers' and pharmacists' names, initials, and facility info to be removed from pill bottle labels. This means Vermont providers can now prescribe and mail abortion pills to patients in non-access states without compromising their privacy. The law is already in effect, offering immediate safeguards for providers and the people they serve.

**_Colorado: Expanded Coverage and Shield Protections_**

Colorado enacted two powerful new reproductive rights laws—a massive win for abortion access and provider protection. One law cements that, starting January 1, 2026, Medicaid enrollees and public employees will have the full cost of abortion care covered for the first time in forty years. This is huge news, especially for low-income Coloradans who’ve long been forced to pay out of pocket for essential care. The second law, which takes effect immediately, strengthens Colorado’s telehealth shield protections in two critical ways: it allows providers’ names to be removed from pill bottle labels mailed to patients in hostile states, and it bars private entities like hospitals from sharing information or cooperating with out-of-state investigations.

From confronting restrictive abortion policies to championing equity on the global stage, we are dedicated to creating a future where everyone has access to the health care they deserve. Here's a snapshot of our most recent efforts: | Global | | Photo Credit: ©Lina Gasca / Trineo Comunicaciones | In the 1990s, thousands of women in Peru—mostly Indigenous, rural, and low-income—were forcibly sterilized under a government policy implemented under former President Alberto Fujimori. Among them was 34-year-old Celia Ramos, who died in 1997 after undergoing a surgical sterilization she had not validly consented to. This month, the Center for Reproductive Rights and partners Study for the Defense of Women's Rights (DEMUS) and the Center for Justice and International Law (CEJIL), argued Celia's case before the Inter-American Court of Human Rights (IACtHR), marking the first time the Court will hear a case on Peru's forced sterilization policy. The Center asked the Court to recognize forced sterilization as a form of reproductive and gender-based violence, and to establish reparations for victims like Celia. The case also seeks concrete measures to ensure this abuse never happens again, such as strengthened consent protections in reproductive health care. "Forced sterilizations were acts of power—and of violence—against the most vulnerable women in Peru," said Catalina Martínez Coral, the Center's Vice President for Latin America and the Caribbean. "Celia Ramos's case presents the Court with the opportunity to set clear standards for States to follow in finally addressing Peru's history of forced sterilization and reproductive violence." | | United States | | | Michigan: Court Strikes Down Harmful Restrictions A Michigan court struck down three abortion restrictions, ruling that they violate the state's voter-approved constitutional amendment safeguarding abortion rights. The Center brought this case on behalf of Northland Family Planning Centers and Medical Students for Choice , challenging laws that mandated biased "counseling," required patients to wait 24 hours before accessing abortion care, and prohibited qualified clinicians from providing care. Judge Sima Patel agreed that these laws were unconstitutional and rejected the state's argument that they were necessary for patient safety. This is a huge win for evidence-based, patient-centered care. Vermont: A Shield Law Breakthrough In May, Vermont passed VT S.28, a strong expansion of abortion care privacy and shield protections for providers. The Center helped draft and advocate for this bill in collaboration with local providers. The law updates telemedicine policy to allow asynchronous patient-provider relationships and allows prescribers' and pharmacists' names, initials, and facility info to be removed from pill bottle labels. This means Vermont providers can now prescribe and mail abortion pills to patients in non-access states without compromising their privacy. The law is already in effect, offering immediate safeguards for providers and the people they serve. Colorado: Expanded Coverage and Shield Protections Colorado enacted two powerful new reproductive rights laws—a massive win for abortion access and provider protection. One law cements that, starting January 1, 2026, Medicaid enrollees and public employees will have the full cost of abortion care covered for the first time in forty years. This is huge news, especially for low-income Coloradans who’ve long been forced to pay out of pocket for essential care. The second law, which takes effect immediately, strengthens Colorado’s telehealth shield protections in two critical ways: it allows providers’ names to be removed from pill bottle labels mailed to patients in hostile states, and it bars private entities like hospitals from sharing information or cooperating with out-of-state investigations. | | | | Anti-abortion members of Congress are working to dismantle a critical protection for reproductive health care providers and patients: the . This federal law prohibits the use of force, threats, and physical obstruction against individuals seeking or providing reproductive health services—including abortion and fertility care. On May 17, just days before the House Judiciary Committee took up the bill, a fertility clinic in Palm Springs, California, was bombed—an alarming reminder of the threats providers face every day. | | | "The history of violence against reproductive health centers is why clinics need protections and patients must feel safe. That's why Congress passed the FACE Act over 30 years ago and why it needs to be strengthened and enforced, not repealed as some in Congress are pushing for." —Nancy Northup, President & CEO Front Lines is dedicated to keeping you informed about the global fight for reproductive rights. 🌍💬 | | | | | ---|---|---|--- The Center for Reproductive Rights uses the power of law to advance reproductive rights as fundamental human rights around the world. © Center for Reproductive Rights Center for Reproductive Rights 199 Water St. New York, NY 10038 United States

For the first time since 2017, Florida will not have a tax holiday on hurricane supplies before the start of hurricane season.
This year's Atlantic hurricane season is projected to be [an above-average year for tropical cyclone activity](https://substack.com/redirect/5104d7db-9988-4c06-9427-26432feb0eaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Yet, Republican infighting on the state's budget has delayed any potential tax holiday for critical hurricane supplies.
[Click here to find/contact your FL reps](https://substack.com/redirect/0e17c4d2-c946-48e5-83e7-e0fd140d32e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A Republican Florida Congresswoman told me today that "everything" is up for cuts this year, including the annual hurricane supplies tax holiday.
The state legislature reconvenes next week to continue work on the budget.
Florida's base sales tax rate is 6%. The sales tax holiday for hurricane supplies, which includes everything from batteries to pet travel supplies, enables families living on a tight budget to make these necessary purchases at a reduced cost...

Peter, We’re a nation of immigrants who for generations have come to our shores because of the promise of freedom, democracy and the American Dream. But yesterday, I personally witnessed something straight out of an authoritarian dictatorship: masked, plain-clothes Gestapo-like ICE agents arresting non-violent, non-criminal asylum applicants coming out of court in order to deport them before they can respond. In a new, coordinated strategy solely designed to increase the total number of deportations, DHS lawyers are doing an end run around our immigration laws by dismissing ongoing deportation proceedings — which often include lawful asylum claims — in order to invoke a different, “expedited” deportation authority to terrorize and remove immigrants following all of the proper procedures. **This xenophobic purge is cruel, cynical and, most importantly, un-American. Today, I confronted these masked ICE agents detaining immigrants who did not have lawyers nor spoke English.** To be very clear, asylum is a lawful pathway to enter the United States. Yet the Trump Administration is using procedural shenanigans to void the asylum claims long enough to deport as many immigrants as possible. Many of these immigrants have work visas, pay social security and income taxes, and have families. This cruelty and xenophobia is not what this nation has stood for throughout our history. These people are not “murderers” or “child rapists,” as Trump falsely claims; they are people voluntarily showing up in court to be lawfully admitted into the country. The Trump Administration has sold the American people a false bill of goods. And I will continue exposing their lawlessness until they stop this nonsense. **[And I need your help. subject: Republicans are cutting Medicaid. Tina’s expanding care.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Tina Kotek

Tina’s delivering on housing, health care, and education for Oregon. |
#
---
Peter, In D.C., Republicans in Congress are pushing cuts to Medicaid and SNAP, jeopardizing health care and food access for millions of families just to hand out more tax breaks to the rich. But here in Oregon, Tina’s showing us what real leadership looks like: putting people first, solving problems, and delivering results that actually improve lives. Take a look at what Tina’s been getting done for Oregon:
* **Invested hundreds of millions of dollars to tackle the housing crisis** — getting people off the streets and into homes.
* **Expanded behavioral health care with $25 million in new funding,** so more Oregonians, especially young people and underserved communities, can get mental health and addiction treatment.
* **Boosted public school funding** so that every child in Oregon gets the education they deserve, no matter their zip code.

Congressional Republicans are telling us where their priorities lie with their shameful and cruel bill. Tina’s showing us with results. clean_body: Tina’s delivering on housing, health care, and education for Oregon. | Peter, In D.C., Republicans in Congress are pushing cuts to Medicaid and SNAP, jeopardizing health care and food access for millions of families just to hand out more tax breaks to the rich. But here in Oregon, Tina’s showing us what real leadership looks like: putting people first, solving problems, and delivering results that actually improve lives. Take a look at what Tina’s been getting done for Oregon: Invested hundreds of millions of dollars to tackle the housing crisis — getting people off the streets and into homes. Expanded behavioral health care with $25 million in new funding, so more Oregonians, especially young people and underserved communities, can get mental health and addiction treatment. Boosted public school funding so that every child in Oregon gets the education they deserve, no matter their zip code. Congressional Republicans are telling us where their priorities lie with their shameful and cruel bill. Tina’s showing us with results. She’s fighting for progress, for working families, and for Oregon’s future — and she needs us with her. [ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/62?t=1001&akid=8636%2E5257348%2EsRSVMt ]Adam Schiff for Senate

Derek, I want
to share this photo with you today and tell you the story alongside it.

This is me at 13 years old, in all my “glory” at my Bar Mitzvah:

[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=q22025_abs_em.gs9A_9&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_GEN_AC90_20250530_AM1_V1_S1&t=1004&akid=8636%2E5257348%2EsRSVMt ]Adam before his bar mitzvah at 13 years old

I’ll admit, it’s easy to laugh at this photo — the classic 1970s bow tie,
the braces, the yarmulke, the looks — but it also gives me an opportunity
to tell you a little about how I approach my faith.

Throughout my career in public service, I’ve thought a lot about the
Jewish tradition of “Tikkun Olam,” or repairing the world. And over the
last few years, a lot has been broken, and there’s a lot to fix. It’s been
my cause.

I want to take you back to 1973. Our family moved around a lot because my
father was in the “schmata” business. He started as a traveling salesman
and later worked as a regional manager for a men’s clothing company.

We moved from Massachusetts, where I was born, lived a few years in
Arizona, and then ended up in the Bay Area. It was there that my dad got
out of the clothing business and bought a lumber yard, where I worked
during the summers. There’s nothing like hauling sheets of plywood and
roofing, and shoveling concrete to make you want to go to graduate school.

This photo is from a time when my family was a member of Temple Isaiah in
Lafayette, California, a reform synagogue we joined after moving to the
Bay Area. And it came after months of practicing for my Bar Mitzvah. I
even taped my practice sessions on our tape recorder (I have a copy of
that tape somewhere, believe it or not, voice cracking and all).

While the Hebrew language skills I quickly acquired were just as quickly
lost, the lessons that my faith taught me endure and guide me to this day.

In fact, my favorite passage comes from Micah: What is required of us, but
to do justice, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God.

These principles have guided my public service. They have led me to pursue
criminal justice reform, to make housing the homeless a key priority, to
combat discrimination, and to ensure the rule of law is applied equally.
They have also guided my path as I held Trump accountable and stood up to
the most unscrupulous man to ever occupy the Oval Office.

And they guide me in the fight we face today: repairing and rebuilding our
democracy so that we leave it better for my children and yours.

That’s why I put everything I have into my work for the cause of our
democracy. It’s the first thing I think about when I wake up in the
morning, and I don’t rest until I’ve done all I can for the day.

name: Dan Crenshaw
subject: Read My Breitbart Op-Ed on Protecting Children From Trans Ideology
body:
This is a major win for our children, for taxpayers, and for common sense.
| | | |
---
| | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01JWGYSP8FEGC9YVK27C0GFT73_0)
---
|
---
| Peter, As you know, protecting America’s children from the excesses of the radical left’s transgender ideology has been one of my top priorities in Congress. I have been at the tip of the spear in fighting back against an ideology that treats our children like lab rats, exposing them to irreversible procedures and treatments that can destroy their lives.
In the Big Beautiful Bill we passed through the House last week to advance President Trump’s agenda, I was proud to secure a significant policy win that will go a long way toward protecting our kids. Under my amendment - the Crenshaw Amendment - taxpayer funded health care programs like Medicaid, CHIP, and the Affordable Care Act will be prohibited from being used for any type of transgender “care.”
This is a major win for our children, for taxpayers, and for common sense. A big reason why this is such a priority for me is that I’ve heard from the very people this policy is designed to protect: those who’ve detransitioned and are now sharing their stories.
One of the most compelling testimonies comes from Chloe Cole. Chloe started transitioning at 12 and regretted it by 16. Now Chloe Cole is fighting to protect kids from the same fate, and we’re turning that fight into federal law with the Crenshaw Amendment.
We recently wrote an op-ed for Breitbart talking about why this fight is so important. I hope you’ll read it. In service,
---
| | |
---
| Dan Crenshaw
---
|
---
| | [ ](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01JWGYSP8FEGC9YVK27C0GFT73_1)
---
| [Exclusive—Rep. Dan Crenshaw and Chloe Cole: The Big Beautiful Bill Protects Children and Taxpayers from Radical Gender Ideology](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01JWGYSP8FEGC9YVK27C0GFT73_2)
---
| The “Big Beautiful Bill” will accomplish a lot, including reigniting America’s economy and keeping your tax rates low. But perhaps one of the most important things it does may be getting overlooked. It bans the use of taxpayer funds in Medicaid, the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP), and Affordable Care Act for transgender procedures. Put simply: it protects vulnerable kids and American taxpayers. For years, we have both led the charge to keep kids safe from radical gender ideology, one of us from Congress and one of us from the trenches of the public square. Rep. Crenshaw authored the Crenshaw Amendment specifically for the “Big Beautiful Bill,” which prohibits taxpayer funding for puberty blockers, cross-sex hormones, and sex-change surgeries. And Ms. Cole is herself a victim of radical gender ideology, having tried to transition genders starting at age 12—only to regret it by age 16. No one knows this fact better than Chloe Cole. Children should never be subjected to this medical assault on their developing body and mind. Encouraged by radicalized medical “professionals,” these transgender procedures are invasive and irreversible, leading to a lifetime of complications and additional health problems. Children, lacking the mental and physical maturity to make life-altering decisions, simply cannot understand the consequences of these procedures—not in the short term and especially not in the long term. True “consent,” as we would normally understand the term, cannot exist under these circumstances. This is common sense. First of all, most Americans agree with these simple statements. But the scientific consensus also backs our position. Various systematic reviews of the evidence came to the same scientific conclusions: low quality evidence of any benefits, with immense risks. And yet, the medical establishment, like so many other parts of society, has been overtaken by activists masquerading as “experts.” They’re putting ideology ahead of ethics, and children across America are paying the price for the leftist activists’ arrogance. No taxpayer should be forced to cover the cost of these procedures. Doing so makes Americans complicit in the destruction of children’s minds and bodies. When people pay taxes, they assume they’re funding things like national security and the safety net. They don’t think they’re paying for a misguided doctor to cut off the genitalia of a confused child. The only thing taxpayers should cover in that situation is real mental health care. To his credit, President Trump has already taken strong steps to protect children and taxpayers from radical gender ideology. He has [issued an executive order](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01JWGYSP8FEGC9YVK27C0GFT73_3) that prohibits the use of taxpayer funding for sex changes. He has also directed his administration to [investigate](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01JWGYSP8FEGC9YVK27C0GFT73_4) those who put children at risk. Most recently, the Trump administration released its own [sweeping review](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01JWGYSP8FEGC9YVK27C0GFT73_5) of the evidence surrounding pediatric transgender procedures. The short version: There’s no real evidence of benefits to children—but there’s reams of evidence showing that kids are being irreparably harmed. These are steps in the right direction, but the “Big Beautiful Bill” is the most important step of all. Until the Crenshaw Amendment and further restrictions are written into federal law, a future president can simply undo the protections that President Trump has put in place. Congress must do its part to make this permanent. This isn’t some fringe issue, by the way. The medical nonprofit [Do No Harm](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01JWGYSP8FEGC9YVK27C0GFT73_6) has [found](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01JWGYSP8FEGC9YVK27C0GFT73_7) that 14,000 kids between 2019 and 2023 alone have already been subjected to dangerous transgender procedures, many of them using taxpayer funds. With a federal law in place, taxpayers and parents can rest easier. Know this: we are winning, but the fight isn’t over. The Crenshaw Amendment is a giant leap forward, and this is our chance to pass it and do what is right for our children. Dan Crenshaw represents Texas’s 2nd congressional district in the U.S. House of Representatives. Chloe Cole is the patient advocate at [Do No Harm](https://ctrk.klclick1.com/l/01JWGYSP8FEGC9YVK27C0GFT73_8).

name: Chris Pappas
subject: I’m running for Senate
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Dignity of Work PAC
body:
I’ll always put New Hampshire first.
| | |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/108659387/548609958/1609710299?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk34-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYzcyZjBkYS02ZjNkLWYwMTEtYTVmMS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=D-CBc53btNSc-zUPY7oR2dCJwZaqSH8r273MXf1net8=)
Friend, I’m Congressman Chris Pappas, and the Dignity of Work PAC said I could reach out with some big news:

**I’m officially running to be New Hampshire’s next U.S. senator.** I’m going to share more about why I’m in this race, but if you’re already on board,**[split a contribution to my campaign and the Dignity of Work PAC today.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/108659391/548609962/1609710299?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk34-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYzcyZjBkYS02ZjNkLWYwMTEtYTVmMS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=D-CBc53btNSc-zUPY7oR2dCJwZaqSH8r273MXf1net8=)**
I’m running for Senate because at this pivotal moment, our economy, our democracy, and our way of life are on the line. New Hampshire deserves a senator who is grounded in the people, places, and values of this state – and one who is ready to lead on day one.

Our country is at a crossroads, and the decisions we make now will have generational impacts. You can count on me to continue taking on big fights and to confront the Trump administration, self-dealing billionaires, and extreme politicians who are threatening our future and our ability to get things done for New Hampshire.
**[Friend, can I count on you to become a Founding Donor to my campaign with a $5 contribution, split between my campaign and the Dignity of Work PAC right now? We can’t win this race without major grassroots support.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/108659395/548609966/1609710299?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=jtk34-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYzcyZjBkYS02ZjNkLWYwMTEtYTVmMS02MDQ1YmRhOWQ5NmIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=D-CBc53btNSc-zUPY7oR2dCJwZaqSH8r273MXf1net8=)**
**These fights are deeply personal to me.** My family immigrated from Greece and opened a restaurant in Manchester 108 years ago, a small business that remains at the heart of the community today. Running that small business showed me the power of hard work and serving others, but the opportunity that my ancestors and so many others like them sought has never been further away – and the Trump administration is too busy cutting deals for their billionaire buddies to give a damn.
I’m also openly gay and happily married to my husband, Vann. With the current wave of hateful policies leveled at the LGBTQ+ community, I know how important representation is at this moment. **If elected, I’d be the first openly gay male U.S. senator in history** – a badge of honor I’d wear proudly as I advocate for full equality.
I am the proud product of public education, and I come from a family of business owners (_my grandfather invented the chicken tender at the restaurant – seriously!_). I understand firsthand the need to support neighborhood schools and small businesses in our community. **These are the lifeblood of our economy and the pillars of opportunity for everyone.**
My life experiences are what led me to successfully run for four terms in Congress and win in one of the “swingiest” districts in the nation. Before I won my election in 2018, no one had managed to hold the seat for more than one term for more than a decade. I’m no stranger to tough electoral fights. **Now I’m ready to take on the fight to keep New Hampshire’s Senate seat blue.**
We can’t afford to sit on the sidelines of the big fights ahead – not with so much at stake, from the rising costs debilitating working families to the threats to the future of our democracy. We’ve taken on big fights together in Congress. Now it’s time to win this critical Senate seat so we can keep standing up to the Trump administration and the self-dealing billionaires threatening our future. Can I count on you to join the fight?
**[Friend, if you’re with me, let’s make a powerful statement together and prove that we’re ready to win this race. name: Ilhan Omar
subject: It’s been five years since George Floyd’s murder
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ILHAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=1656%2E791427%2E2mvhqB)

Friend,
This week marks five years since George Floyd’s murder. He should be alive today. No amount of grandstanding or rewriting history will change that fact.
On this day — and every day — we must commit ourselves to the pursuit of justice. That must include dismantling systemic racism and radically transforming our approach to criminal justice.
His murder ignited urgent conversations about the state of our nation, the state of policing, and the state of our justice system — as well as who is entitled to justice.
And unfortunately, as we have seen every time there is a movement for the liberation of Black people, for equality, for justice, we see a backslide — a backlash — where things not only stop progressing, but where people are emboldened to express their racism publicly.
_We even are seeing unjust calls for Chauvin to be pardoned._
Regardless of any federal pardon, he still faces the state murder conviction and will remain in jail. He will always be known to the people of this country and the world as a murderer.
We still have a lot of work before we see true justice and liberation.
But this week I’m thinking of George Floyd’s family as they continue to grieve his loss.
May he forever rest in power.
In solidarity,
Ilhan Omar
* * *

name: Gretchen Whitmer
subject: Why I keep fighting — and I hope you will too
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Fight Like Hell PAC
body:
When people count you out, you show up anyway. |
#
---
Team — When I first ran for office, a lot of people told me not to do it. Some said I was too young. Others said the timing wasn’t right. More than a few told me that a woman couldn’t win. But I knew why I was running. I believed in what I stood for, and I refused to let cynicism make decisions for me. I’ve never forgotten that feeling, which is why I believe so deeply in the work of Fight Like Hell PAC. Because every day, there are people out there who are told the same things I once was. That they’re not the right fit. That politics is broken. That it’s just not worth it. **But it _is_ worth it.** Public service matters. Good things happen when the right people say yes. And we’ve seen the cost when they don’t. That’s why we’re working to bring new people into this fight. We’re helping everyday folks step into leadership, connect with their communities, and build the tools they need to run — and win. I know it can be tempting to give up or tune out, especially in the moment we find ourselves in. clean_body: When people count you out, you show up anyway. | Team — When I first ran for office, a lot of people told me not to do it. Some said I was too young. Others said the timing wasn’t right. More than a few told me that a woman couldn’t win. But I knew why I was running. I believed in what I stood for, and I refused to let cynicism make decisions for me. I’ve never forgotten that feeling, which is why I believe so deeply in the work of Fight Like Hell PAC. Because every day, there are people out there who are told the same things I once was. That they’re not the right fit. That politics is broken. That it’s just not worth it. But it is worth it. Public service matters. Good things happen when the right people say yes. And we’ve seen the cost when they don’t. That’s why we’re working to bring new people into this fight. We’re helping everyday folks step into leadership, connect with their communities, and build the tools they need to run — and win. I know it can be tempting to give up or tune out, especially in the moment we find ourselves in. https://www.lateefahsimon.com [https://www.lateefahsimon.com]
Friend,
As the Congresswoman for Oakland, Berkeley, Emeryville, Piedmont, Albany, Alameda, and San Leandro, I consider it both my privilege and duty to bring the voices and needs of working-class, diverse communities straight into the halls of power where people like us have historically been left behind.
I’ve been an organizer for over 30 years, so I know what it takes to bring communities together, hold the powerful accountable, and demand results.
That’s why I asked my team to create a quick form for you to fill out on what issues you’re most concerned about, how Congress can better serve you, and if you’ve been affected by the Trump administration. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/y_xac2qEAUuOlWCDgNCPdA2]
At every step — whether we’re fighting for affordable health care access, education programs, or accessible transit — I know that the people closest to the pain are also closest to the solutions, and we need to use every tool in the toolbox to create solutions. This survey will help us to hear directly from the folks who matter most: the organizers, caregivers, riders, and neighbors like you in our communities - so we can continue lifting up your voices in Congress.

Hi there,
All across Michigan, I’m seeing incredible energy and enthusiasm from people ready to make our state the best place to be a kid, raise a kid, and call home.
Thank you to everyone who’s taken the time to talk with me about my vision to ensure every Michigander can thrive. This is how we shape Michigan’s next decade — by coming together and building a future we can all believe in.

Now, it’s our job to make sure what happened in last year’s election does not define Michigan for decades to come. It’s time to stand up and protect our progress, because we know that history is on our side. The law and the Constitution are on our side.

Peter Willis,

BREAKING: The moment we've been fearing has arrived: the White House
confirmed it will send an official request to Congress to defund NPR and
PBS NEXT WEEK. And House Speaker Johnson has vowed to act quickly to bring
it to a vote.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/30875?source=email-20250530&t=1011&akid=8585%2E5885482%2E4eon6m ]Headline: Trump to ask Congress to codify DOGE cuts, hitting PBS and
NPR

Make no mistake: Trump's attempt to silence our public broadcasters is a
direct attack on independent journalism and educational programming that
millions across America rely upon. We CANNOT let it happen!

The good news is Congress KNOWS just how popular and vital public media is
to our communities, and even some Republicans have expressed concerns with
Trump’s war on PBS and NPR.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/30876?source=email-20250530&t=1012&akid=8585%2E5885482%2E4eon6m ]Now it’s up to ALL of us to overwhelm our representatives with demands
to save public media. Click here RIGHT NOW to tell Congress: Vote no on
Trump's dangerous DOGE cuts package!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/30876?source=email-20250530&t=1013&akid=8585%2E5885482%2E4eon6m ]ADD YOUR NAME

The White House just confirmed that Trump’s DOGE package – which will claw
back $9.4 billion in funding that Congress ALREADY approved – will be sent
to the Hill early next week.

If these reckless cuts pass, communities across America will lose vital
public broadcast stations – the sole providers of in-depth, independent,
community-oriented reporting in many regions.

We don’t have much time, which is why we need to flood lawmakers’ inboxes
immediately with a clear message: we will not stand by as Trump claws back
critical funds in the name of "government efficiency." Speaker Johnson is
betting on minimal resistance – let's prove him wrong and stop this
reckless plan in its tracks.

Click below to send an urgent message to your representatives today
demanding they vote NO on Trump’s dangerous DOGE package – and protect
public broadcasting for millions of Americans depending on it every day.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/30876?source=email-20250530&t=1014&akid=8585%2E5885482%2E4eon6m ]Tell Congress: Defend NPR & PBS – Vote against Trump’s reckless funding
cuts!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/30876?source=email-20250530&t=1015&akid=8585%2E5885482%2E4eon6m ]ADD YOUR NAME

This isn’t just a battle about financial allocations – it’s a defense of
independent media that holds politicians accountable, investigates
injustices, and keeps us connected, educated, and engaged.

Our movement has come together time and time again to defend public media
– and we’re not stopping now.

When we organize, we win.

| A two-year old U.S. citizen, born in Florida to two undocumented parents, was deported by ICE alongside her parents to Brazil where she does not have legal status - leaving her without a country to call home. The 14th amendment of the Constitution grants citizenship to all persons born or naturalized in the United States, making her deportation a gross violation of the constitution and basic humanity.
This isn't the first time the Trump administration has deported children. Last month children aged 2,4, and 7 were sent to Honduras with their undocumented parents. One of the kids had cancer and was shipped away without medication.
Just weeks ago, Gov. Tim Walz got heat from the Trump administration for comparing ICE to the Gestapo - but he was right. In just the first few months of Trump's administration, ICE has deported children with U.S. citizenship, sent unmarked cars and masked agents to arrest foreign students who protest, sent migrants with legal status to El Salvadorian torture prisons without due process, and even detained a mother moments after giving birth.

clean_body: Just when you think things couldn’t get worse, news breaks that reminds you we’re living in Donald Trump’s fascist America now. | | | | | == | Friend Just when you think things couldn't get worse, news breaks that reminds you we're living in Donald Trump's fascist America now: | | == | A two-year old U.S. citizen, born in Florida to two undocumented parents, was deported by ICE alongside her parents to Brazil where she does not have legal status - leaving her without a country to call home. The 14th amendment of the Constitution grants citizenship to all persons born or naturalized in the United States, making her deportation a gross violation of the constitution and basic humanity. This isn't the first time the Trump administration has deported children. Last month children aged 2,4, and 7 were sent to Honduras with their undocumented parents. One of the kids had cancer and was shipped away without medication. Just weeks ago, Gov. Tim Walz got heat from the Trump administration for comparing ICE to the Gestapo - but he was right. In just the first few months of Trump's administration, ICE has deported children with U.S. citizenship, sent unmarked cars and masked agents to arrest foreign students who protest, sent migrants with legal status to El Salvadorian torture prisons without due process, and even detained a mother moments after giving birth. | | == | ICE is an instrument in Trump's fascism - a tool used to crush dissent, inflict terror on marginalized communities, and appease white supremacists. ICE should not exist, it is a product of the infamous Patriot Act - the bill passed by Congress after 9/11 that drastically increased the power of law enforcement at the detriment of our civil liberties. When the Patriot Act was passed, critics rightfully panned the law for its potential to be abused by a cruel and corrupt President. It only took two decades for that President to emerge, Donald Trump, and he is using ICE as his personal Gestapo. National Ground Game PAC is fighting back against this fascist administration. body:
#
Donald Trump’s White House attacked Alexandria on Wednesday!
This isn’t new. Donald Trump, Fox News, and other right-wing MAGA Republicans are _obsessed_ with Alexandria.
**This attack is a distraction.** Trump is trying to divert attention away from the fact that **House Republicans just voted to kick 13.7 million people off of their healthcare** and stole food assistance from 11 million folks to give tax cuts to billionaires.
We’re intentionally not going into detail here because it would only give MAGA more things to be faux-outraged about.
Alexandria ran for Congress not from the left or the right, _but from the bottom._ She’s working to demand better for all of us and to fight for racial, social, environmental and economic justice.
**How we respond to Trump’s attack at this moment is incredibly important.**

Get to know United States v. Bhagat Singh Thind (1923), a landmark court case that shed light on the intersection of racial injustice and nationalism in the U.S.

Bhagat Singh Thind, an Indian Sikh and World War I veteran, applied for U.S. citizenship under the Naturalization Act of 1906. This Act limited eligibility to "free white persons" and people of African descent.

Thind argued that as an Indian of Aryan descent, he qualified as “Caucasian” based on the scientific classifications of the time.

The Supreme Court rejected this argument. Instead the Court ruled that the term "white person" referred to “the common understanding of the average white American.”

Therefore, despite his service to the country, Thind was deemed ineligible for citizenship. The decision not only denied his request for citizenship, but also led to the withdrawal of citizenship of other Indian Americans who had previously been granted U.S. citizenship.

The ruling shed light on how race is socially constructed, not scientific. The Supreme Court ruling reinforced that race in U.S. law was subjective and exclusionary, often aligning with white supremacy.

Although this ruling upheld racial barriers, it also inspired public resistance and awareness moving forward.

Over time, reforms like the Luce-Celler Act of 1946 and the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965 dismantled race-based immigration restrictions.

Bhagat Singh Thind (1923), a landmark court case that shed light on the intersection of racial injustice and nationalism in the U.S. Bhagat Singh Thind, an Indian Sikh and World War I veteran, applied for U.S. citizenship under the Naturalization Act of 1906. This Act limited eligibility to "free white persons" and people of African descent. Thind argued that as an Indian of Aryan descent, he qualified as “Caucasian” based on the scientific classifications of the time. The Supreme Court rejected this argument. Instead the Court ruled that the term "white person" referred to “the common understanding of the average white American.” Therefore, despite his service to the country, Thind was deemed ineligible for citizenship. The decision not only denied his request for citizenship, but also led to the withdrawal of citizenship of other Indian Americans who had previously been granted U.S. citizenship. The ruling shed light on how race is socially constructed, not scientific. The Supreme Court ruling reinforced that race in U.S. law was subjective and exclusionary, often aligning with white supremacy. body:
Here’s just some of what you may have missed in the 1,000 page mega bill: | | | Peter, Last week, the Republican-controlled House narrowly passed Trump’s “big, beautiful” bill — which was anything but. It takes a cleaver to Medicaid, food stamps, and clean energy initiatives, while of course giving massive tax giveaways to billionaires. But that’s not all. **In addition to being a giant gift to the billionaire class at the expense of everyone else, there are a ton of other provisions that Republicans slipped into this bill that would be disastrous for the working class.** We wanted to take a few minutes here to highlight some of the worst of them, but before we do: [**Can you add your name to our petition to urge your elected officials to oppose Trump’s budget bill? With Congress on recess, and the bill due to start making its way through the Senate in a matter of weeks, we need to keep the pressure on.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoe1DuqQbjt4KoloTZxD-XRIq_Rq3KohZ4y2Iu5_arjN96GU-x7mp3w8PmRLxAlpgPKXeE6w4Kro5K6LrL9gEC0TW7vLW5ZQyOMCP4FH87cDL2AIWr1w1eLAS6UfiJA_1MBNegZqzqJG9_h1dzv71yC4RDNhCjMArzmBTqoCZ_tLFn3n-vOCNjXQeAGjdgSd7FIoGS--PzTXxxe0iYr_oSmXdo2AQEeO8t3Hq3dOEYvENBXXoR-G1Bt4__XGrXvaBgppZ9HhQ4IRKB02z-xL1Y89TIITI7UvLC3Vb_Tg1KiDyBX_dfl_CaGZVfYYNaKliNf02NTDzQbk4p53BAPG30o0/4gx/ubdX8Z99QK2Vz-3fRKqtFg/h0/h001.fBSsQzd49HNCSk6py_wEjwOQ_-e-d8hhG255qPS8i50) The attacks on Medicaid and giveaways to billionaires may have been what made the headlines about this budget. But the bill that passed the House last week also massively increases our defense spending, attacks our democracy and system of checks and balances, and makes it harder for working families to make ends meet. Here’s just some of what you may have missed in the 1,000 page mega bill:1
* More funding for Trump’s mass deportation operation, including spending $46.5 billion on Trump’s border wall
* A splurge of $150 billion in additional spending for our already bloated Defense budget including Trump’s “Golden Dome,” which experts have called “a dangerous fantasy”2
* Changes to student loan repayment plans so that students pay more and qualify for less aid3
* Higher prescription costs for seniors under Medicare
* Cuts in funding for Planned Parenthood and a ban on Medicaid from covering transition care
* And more drilling and mining on public lands.

But wait, there’s more:
* Hidden deep in the budget is a provision that would restrict federal courts’ authority to hold government officials in contempt if they violate judicial orders.
* This bill also includes a ten-year ban on regulating artificial intelligence, including restricting states from passing laws to prevent AI from misleading the public with election misinformation.4
* And it gives the Trump admin the ability to define any nonprofit they don’t like as a “terrorist-supporting organization” and ending their tax status — a major threat against freedom of speech.5

**This bill is not only a massive redistribution of wealth from working families to the billionaires — it’s also a sneak attack on democracy itself.** As the bill now makes its way to the Senate, the time is now to make our voices heard. [**Sign our petition to urge your legislators to oppose this massive boondoggle of a bill that only serves Trump and the billionaire class at the expense of everyone else.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoe1DuqQbjt4KoloTZxD-XRIq_Rq3KohZ4y2Iu5_arjN96GU-x7mp3w8PmRLxAlpgPKXeE6w4Kro5K6LrL9gEC0TW7vLW5ZQyOMCP4FH87cDL2AIWr1w1eLAS6UfiJA_1MBNegZqzqJG9_h1dzv71yC4rjWagfNeLtMsSZoYRdsZXN083zRgNEzHp802107z2jNC2BgxAUPBbFygUBy0hPs6FM1kYDbSVfWXOBt7QHXGU8KIvTKY8it0DIJgnzLmP56_4npeZrZYcv9S8rcte7d7rGJy_gqsBASr0xYfP4ckiXZ-i0c7qbWHuYFhyQP5xGoeslIcR119b9R2mgjYiWhA/4gx/ubdX8Z99QK2Vz-3fRKqtFg/h1/h001.uVBzaXC3jzlCrkGDSv6FVxnh0rFd5EN3ryxnMKZ9O4M) In solidarity, Team WFP Source: 1\. clean_body: Here’s just some of what you may have missed in the 1,000 page mega bill: | | | Peter, Last week, the Republican-controlled House narrowly passed Trump’s “big, beautiful” bill — which was anything but. It takes a cleaver to Medicaid, food stamps, and clean energy initiatives, while of course giving massive tax giveaways to billionaires. But that’s not all. In addition to being a giant gift to the billionaire class at the expense of everyone else, there are a ton of other provisions that Republicans slipped into this bill that would be disastrous for the working class. We wanted to take a few minutes here to highlight some of the worst of them, but before we do: The attacks on Medicaid and giveaways to billionaires may have been what made the headlines about this budget. But the bill that passed the House last week also massively increases our defense spending, attacks our democracy and system of checks and balances, and makes it harder for working families to make ends meet. Here’s just some of what you may have missed in the 1,000 page mega bill:1 More funding for Trump’s mass deportation operation, including spending $46.5 billion on Trump’s border wall A splurge of $150 billion in additional spending for our already bloated Defense budget including Trump’s “Golden Dome,” which experts have called “a dangerous fantasy”2 Changes to student loan repayment plans so that students pay more and qualify for less aid3 Higher prescription costs for seniors under Medicare Cuts in funding for Planned Parenthood and a ban on Medicaid from covering transition care And more drilling and mining on public lands. But wait, there’s more: Hidden deep in the budget is a provision that would restrict federal courts’ authority to hold government officials in contempt if they violate judicial orders. This bill also includes a ten-year ban on regulating artificial intelligence, including restricting states from passing laws to prevent AI from misleading the public with election misinformation.4 And it gives the Trump admin the ability to define any nonprofit they don’t like as a “terrorist-supporting organization” and ending their tax status — a major threat against freedom of speech.5 This bill is not only a massive redistribution of wealth from working families to the billionaires — it’s also a sneak attack on democracy itself. As the bill now makes its way to the Senate, the time is now to make our voices heard. In solidarity, Team WFP Source: 1\. , The New York Times, May 23, 2025 2\. , Scientific American, May 22, 2025 3\. , NPR, April 30, 2025 4\. , Campaign Legal Center, May 22, 2025 5\. , The American Prospect, May 23, 2025 Thoughts? * * *
_**Here’s the situation:**_
California’s clean car rule was the most ambitious of its kind in the nation — a real plan to end the sale of new gas-powered vehicles by 2035. It would have slashed emissions and set a new national standard for climate leadership.
But the Senate just voted to kill it.
_**Here’s why it matters:**_
Republicans in Washington led the charge, and dozens of Democrats helped them. They overturned a policy that could have shifted the course of climate action **and, instead, handed the fossil fuel industry a massive victory at our expense. And the consequences go far beyond one state.**
Eleven other states, along with Washington, D.C., intended to adopt California’s plan and stop selling new gas-powered vehicles by 2035. They understood what’s at stake: Vehicle pollution is one of the largest sources of planet-warming emissions, and this policy was one of the few serious attempts to address it. Now it's been ripped away.
Let’s be clear: This is a direct attack on our right to breathe clean air and live in a world not dictated by oil executives and corporate polluters.
_**Here’s how you can fight back:**_
**We’re counting on the first 1,000 people reading this email to speak out, condemn this egregious rollback of clean energy progress, and show we won’t sit quietly while politicians in Washington choose fossil fuel CEOs over everyday people.**

clean_body: We need to act fast. | URGENT: Senate Republicans delivered a huge blow to climate progress and overturned California’s historic effort to phase out new gas-powered cars by 2035. | Here’s the situation: California’s clean car rule was the most ambitious of its kind in the nation — a real plan to end the sale of new gas-powered vehicles by 2035. It would have slashed emissions and set a new national standard for climate leadership. But the Senate just voted to kill it. Here’s why it matters: Republicans in Washington led the charge, and dozens of Democrats helped them. They overturned a policy that could have shifted the course of climate action and, instead, handed the fossil fuel industry a massive victory at our expense. And the consequences go far beyond one state. Eleven other states, along with Washington, D.C., intended to adopt California’s plan and stop selling new gas-powered vehicles by 2035. They understood what’s at stake: Vehicle pollution is one of the largest sources of planet-warming emissions, and this policy was one of the few serious attempts to address it. Now it's been ripped away. Let’s be clear: This is a direct attack on our right to breathe clean air and live in a world not dictated by oil executives and corporate polluters. Here’s how you can fight back: We’re counting on the first 1,000 people reading this email to speak out, condemn this egregious rollback of clean energy progress, and show we won’t sit quietly while politicians in Washington choose fossil fuel CEOs over everyday people. During my career in law enforcement, I locked up drug dealers, arrested and deported criminals here illegally, and did everything I could to keep the community safe.

**I have some scars to show for it: I was shot and stabbed in the line of duty.**

That didn’t break me; it strengthened my resolve. During my career as a law enforcement officer, I busted criminals, yes, but I also built bridges with diverse communities and saw neighbors helping neighbors.
